title: ESCAPE THANKSKILLING : OH GOD &  MY LORD

sense.text:
“But chiefly them that walk after the flesh in the lust of uncleanness”: that is what it boils down to. Men in captivity now saying you can have concubines, multiple women, slave wives. You are in slavery yourself and you want slaves. You can’t make it up.

“And despise government.” They despise being led. They want to lead when they are not leaders, when they lack the time and the experience to lead. They don’t want an elder over them; they say I am an elder, I am a priest. These are the attributes of men who seek a preeminence they are not worthy of.

“Presumptuous are they”: like saying the elders in the old school taught that the nations are going to be saved, when they were not there. “Selfwilled”: going off on their own and doing whatever they want without any instruction or guidance. “They are not afraid to speak evil of dignities”: they are not afraid to disrespect those that were around before them, to go against their own elders. Deserters, defectors. These are the attributes of such.

“But these, as natural brute beasts, made to be taken and destroyed”: the same ones mentioned before. Some are predestined for death, and their actions and their teachings make it so.

They “speak evil of the things that they understand not”, like saying Paul taught idolatry. But the scriptures say Paul was a chosen vessel, and Paul says he was taught by Christ himself. If he then wrote telling us to serve other gods he would be a false prophet, and brothers would rather be slick about it and say he just made a mistake. A mistake is what Peter did when he denied Christ three times. Telling someone in a letter to reverence another god is far from a mistake; that is idolatry.

If Paul taught idolatry, then Peter, the elder of the disciples, who read all of Paul’s letters, let it stand, and so did the other eleven, and Christ was asleep while it happened. That would mean we serve an incompetent God who chose incompetent disciples. These “shall utterly perish in their own corruption.”

precepts.why:
Peter speaks of Paul’s letters: “As also in all his epistles.” All his epistles. Peter read all of Paul’s letters. When Paul wrote Corinthians, around 54 or 55 AD, Peter was alive, and so were Andrew, John and the other surviving disciples.

In them “are some things hard to be understood”, but see who they are hard for: “which they that are unlearned and unstable wrest.” The same ones Peter described in chapter 2: selfwilled, presumptuous, walking in uncleanness. Unstable: one minute the nations can’t be saved, the next minute they can; they are all wicked, then some of them are good. They wrestle with the letters, they twist them, “as they do also the other scriptures”, the scriptures about the nations going into captivity and not being saved, “unto their own destruction”, which Peter said earlier they are reserved for.

Read on: “seeing ye know these things before, beware lest ye also, being led away with the error of the wicked, fall from your own stedfastness.” So those who are unlearned and unstable with Paul’s letters are in the error of the wicked. That is what Peter says about Paul’s letters, and he never said Paul was off. The steadfastness he speaks of is the teaching of those letters. “But grow in grace, and in the knowledge of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ.”

Jude addresses the same thing: “Likewise also these filthy dreamers defile the flesh, despise dominion, and speak evil of dignities.” They despise being led. They want to be leaders but are not built to be one; they lack the time and the experience. You know them by their actions, by their decorum, by the pride and arrogance in them. Not in the truth twenty years and running their mouth against men who were teaching in the street when they were seven years old.

“But these speak evil of those things which they know not”: speaking evil of leadership that was around long before their time, on the strength of some book of dubious dating. “In those things they corrupt themselves.”

“Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain.” Cain hated his brother. When you teach that your brother’s enemies, the man who destroyed and celebrates the death of your people on this very day, can be saved, that is the spirit of Cain: you hate your people. They “ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward”: Balaam wanted the money. And they “perished in the gainsaying of Core”: the same spirit that said to Moses, you think you are better than us.

sense.text:
These are the rules of engagement when it comes to the Bible. “Whom shall he teach knowledge? and whom shall he make to understand doctrine?” Whom will God teach to understand his Bible, how to speak his words?

“Them that are weaned from the milk, and drawn from the breasts.” Those nourished by their parents, by their elders, by the word of God: they have guidance. A baby can’t teach itself how to drink milk or how to walk. That is why we have elders.

“For precept must be upon precept, precept upon precept; line upon line, line upon line; here a little, and there a little.” It does not say precept upon commentary, precept upon other versions, precept upon the Strong’s. If a commentary or the Strong’s or another version corroborates the precepts, it is usable. If it does not, it is garbage.

There is a new trend in Israel of running to eight versions for one verse, to the NLT and the BSB and the Blue Letter Bible. The elders back then went into Times Square with nothing but the King James and destroyed everything. Under Bishop in 2006 no one was using all these concordances. There is something or someone behind this new adaptation. Stay in the precepts. The Bible is self-explanatory; it doesn’t need help.

precepts.why:
Paul says the exact same thing: “Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth.” Rightly dividing is here a little, there a little.

We listen to Paul because Paul was chosen by Christ; he was no false prophet, and Peter said if you don’t understand Paul’s letters you are in the error of the wicked. When we use the precepts the Christians can’t deal with us. Gentile is in the Bible, Greek is in the Bible, and the Bible explains them. Before there was a concordance or a Strong’s, there were the precepts.

sense.text:
“And I saw a new heaven and a new earth”: this is the kingdom. “For the first heaven and the first earth were passed away”: the kingdoms of the earth, the lower kingdoms, are gone.

“And there was no more sea.” Does that mean no more oceans, no more rivers? No. A commentary won’t tell you what the sea is; the precepts tell you. The sea is the nations, and John saw no more nations. Gone, like a magic trick; that is what God is going to do. A precept-upon-precept class, staying in one version.

precepts.why: “The waters which thou sawest, where the whore sitteth”, where the whore of Babylon sits, “are peoples, and multitudes, and nations, and tongues.” So the sea is nations. See how easy that was? Three chapters over, no Strong’s needed.

To see that waters and seas are the same word in the Old Testament: “Let the waters under the heaven be gathered together unto one place.” The waters under the heaven, because there are waters above the heaven too, deep space; the waters under it are the waters on the earth.

“And the gathering together of the waters called he Seas.” So waters and seas are synonymous, and John said, as a parable, that the waters are the nations.

David prays, “rid me, and deliver me out of great waters, from the hand of strange children.” The great waters are strange children: other nations. That is the sea John saw no more of.

“Whose mouth speaketh vanity, and their right hand is a right hand of falsehood”: the nations. Then “I will sing a new song unto thee, O God”: that is in the kingdom. “It is he that giveth salvation unto kings”, not unto all nations, not unto good nations: unto kings, and the kings are us, “who delivereth David his servant from the hurtful sword.”

So the nations are called great waters, great waters are called seas, and today we call them oceans. Sea and nations are one and the same.

When Christ returns: “God came from Teman”, and Teman is Edom, “and the Holy One from mount Paran.” Keep the Holy One in mind. “he had horns coming out of his hand: and there was the hiding of his power”: beams of power in his hand, holding back a power that could destroy everything.

Read on to verse 8: “Was the Lord displeased against the rivers?” Is Christ coming back mad at the Harlem River? No: “was thy wrath against the sea”, against the nations, “that thou didst ride upon thine horses and thy chariots of salvation?” We will see who those chariots are for.

Verse 12: “thou didst thresh the heathen in anger.” He threshed the heathen; it doesn’t say some good ones. “Thou wentest forth for the salvation of thy people, even for salvation with thine anointed”: not thy people and other good people. Are all nations anointed? No. “Thou woundedst the head out of the house of the wicked”: he cut the head off the main nation, Edom.

“Woe to the multitude of many people, which make a noise like the noise of the seas; and to the rushing of nations, that make a rushing like the rushing of mighty waters!” David said deliver me from great waters; here the nations rush like many waters.

“But God shall rebuke them”, as we just read in Habakkuk 3, “and they shall flee far off, and shall be chased as the chaff of the mountains before the wind.”

“And they shall go into the holes of the rocks, and into the caves of the earth, for fear of the Lord.” The nations shall hide: the last-day preppers, the elites with money, Zuckerberg, Musk, the Arabs, the Asians, with their bunkers under the mountains for when Christ returns, “when he ariseth to shake terribly the earth.” Nuclear destruction.

“In that day a man shall cast his idols of silver, and his idols of gold, which they made each one for himself to worship, to the moles and to the bats; To go into the clefts of the rocks, and into the tops of the ragged rocks, for fear of the Lord.” If they were going to be saved, why are they hiding? Why build bunkers if the Lord is coming to give you salvation?

When the nations run and hide, what do we do? “The Lord liveth, that brought up the children of Israel from the land of the north”: the land of the north is the head of the wicked, the capital, “and from all the lands whither he had driven them.” Israel is scattered all over the world, not only in America; we are an international people.

“Behold, I will send for many fishers, saith the Lord, and they shall fish them.” That is what we are doing now: we travel and fish for our people scattered among the waters, and the waters are nations. “And after will I send for many hunters, and they shall hunt them from every mountain, and from every hill, and out of the holes of the rocks”, where the nations will be hiding.

Nowhere does it say they get saved along with us. They hide, and they are hunted. There is no good Edomite chariot, no good Moabite chariot. There are no good heathen chariots.
“For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect.” Israel is God’s elect. Give one precept where any nation outside the Israelites is called God’s elect. One. There isn’t one.

“Men’s hearts failing them for fear, and for looking after those things which are coming on the earth: for the powers of heaven shall be shaken.” They hide from the shaking because of nuclear destruction. “And then shall they see the Son of man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.”

“And when these things begin to come to pass, then look up”: the chariots are going to show up. “And lift up your heads; for your redemption draweth nigh.” Your redemption. Not everyone’s redemption, not all good nations’ redemption.

The same account, for those who don’t accept Luke because he was not one of the twelve. “Immediately after the tribulation of those days.” That tribulation is Jacob’s trouble. It doesn’t say Jacob and heathen trouble. What trouble are the nations in? This is their world. Why would the Lord save nations from no trouble?

“Shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken”: that is destruction. “And then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.”

“And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.” His elect, and not some good nations. Show one good Edomite, one heathen good to Israel, that God calls his elect. This is house doctrine, trying to save your mama and grandma. You are not saving them.

Christ is going to gather his elect from the four winds: that is his own people. Outside of that you are teaching Christianity. “But they shall serve the Lord their God, and David their king, whom I will raise up unto them.” “Therefore fear thou not, O my servant Jacob, saith the Lord; neither be dismayed, O Israel: for, lo, I will save thee from afar, and thy seed from the land of their captivity; and Jacob shall return, and shall be in rest, and be quiet, and none shall make him afraid.”

Verse 11: “For I am with thee, saith the Lord, to save thee: though I make a full end of all nations whither I have scattered thee.” He will make a full end of all nations. That sounds like what John said: no more sea. Every other version the brothers love to run to says the same, that he will completely destroy the nations where Israel was scattered.

Even an old commentary from 1871 on Obadiah says that in the day of the Lord upon all nations an exact retribution shall be meted out to Edom, that all nations were involved in our captivity, every last one of them, that Edom gets the doom of all, that God’s people get the ultimate salvation, and that the nations who are enemies of God are doomed to extinction. All of them, even the good ones. They know our salvation is their end.

sense.text:
The elders and the people you learn from will determine whether or not you get the kingdom of heaven. A good leader had to first be a follower, had to be taught, had to have elders over him. Joshua was a servant to Moses and then he became a leader. You can’t wake up one morning and say I’m a leader; you have to go through trials and learn to discern good and evil before you fit that position. Twenty years in the truth is twenty years of trials and tribulations and overcoming.

“Not a novice.” A novice is a beginner. Five years, ten years in the truth, you are a novice; fifteen years, you are a teenager. In setting up elders and leaders over a congregation, the scripture says don’t put up novices: young brothers still in their twenties who haven’t been through anything in life.

“Lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the devil.” How does a novice set over a congregation fall into the condemnation of the devil? Satan uses a novice to bring out different doctrines. He whispers in his ears, the novice is deceived, and then he teaches you wrong doctrines. Whoever you follow determines whether you get the right tools to fight, to strive and to endure to get the kingdom.

Flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God. The elect will be changed in the twinkling of an eye, and be equal unto the angels; the nations will not. They will serve their sentence and be gone. After that thousand years the Lord gets rid of all nations, and then the Father himself appears on the earth, and nothing that can sin can be in his presence. This is within that first thousand years.

“There shall be no more thence an infant of days.” It is not talking about babies. An infant of days is being 50, 100, 200 years old: counting your days. The Most High is called the Ancient of days; he has no beginning and no end. With us there will be no more infant of days: we are going to live forever. “Nor an old man that hath not filled his days”, because we will be equal unto the angels.

“For the child shall die an hundred years old”: that is the nations. “But the sinner being an hundred years old shall be accursed.” The sinner is the other nations; they still have that sinful nature in them. The nations who live to see a hundred years will be walking on sticks, crippled, unable to see, the way a man of a hundred is today. It won’t be like that with us. When Christ returns the Lord removes the sinful nature from the elect delivered up out of here.

The apologetics keep trying to battle us with that trinitarian garbage and ask us about the divinity of Christ. This is how you deal with them: “so your minds should be corrupted from the simplicity that is in Christ.” The simplicity that is in Christ is the simple things about Christ.

They don’t understand the simple things. Christ is a black man; Christ came from the negroes here in America; that is who Christ came and died for. If they can’t understand what Christ looks like, if they don’t even know who they are, they are not going to understand his divinity. Don’t even try to explain it to them. But in this class the divinity of Christ is explained for you.

precepts.why:
“But the natural man receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God.” The natural man is the sinful man; the natural man is the Christians. They can’t receive it. “For they are foolishness unto him”: explain it to them and they will think you are foolish. “Neither can he know them.”

“Because they are spiritually discerned.” The spirit of Christ has to be dwelling in you for you to understand his divinity, and the spirit dwelling in these Christians is not the spirit of Christ; it is the spirit of antichrist, the spirit of the devil. Unless they repent and wake up to the truth that they are the children of Israel, and the Holy Spirit dwells in them, they won’t understand. So don’t waste your time explaining the divinity of Christ to a Christian.

sense.text:
This is the divinity of Christ: Oh my God and my Lord. It is a lot, and for those who are new it will be difficult; go back over it later.

“In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.” That is the part wanted: the God there. The same God that made everything in the beginning says in verse 26, “Let us make man in our image.” Who is the “our”? The Father and the Son.

The Word that was with God is the God that created everything, which is the Son. The Father used his Son to make everything. Christ is his Father’s Word: when the Father spoke, the Son was made, and what the Father says is done because his Son is doing it.

precepts.why:
“And God said”: the same God that made everything in the beginning. “Let us make man in our image, after our likeness.” Who is the “our” here? That question is answered in John 1: the Father and the Son.

That is where the rest began, which comes up later in the class.

“In the beginning”: that is what Moses said. “Was the Word”, capital W, “and the Word was with God.” The Word was with God: that is the “our” of “Let us make man in our image”, the Father and the Son. “And the Word was God”: the God that created everything, which is the Son.

“The same was in the beginning with God.” The same Word was in the beginning with God; therefore, let us make man in our image, the image of the Father and his Son.

It was read again after Ecclesiasticus 24:3, “I came out of the mouth of the most High”, to show that this is why Christ is called the Word of God.

“Doth not wisdom cry? and understanding put forth her voice?” Some will argue it says her, so it can’t be Christ, because Christ is not a woman. But what is the book called? Proverbs. Interesting name, and it is answered later.

Verse 9: “They are all plain to him that understandeth.” That is what Paul said: they are spiritually discerned. You understand when you keep God’s commandments; that is the simplicity in Christ too. Verse 12: “I wisdom dwell with prudence.” The context from verse 1 to 12 does not change: wisdom.

Verse 22: “The Lord possessed me in the beginning of his way, before his works of old.” Wisdom was around before things were made. “I was set up from everlasting, from the beginning, or ever the earth was”: before the earth was made, because the Father used his Son to make everything. “When there were no depths, I was brought forth”: brought forth is begotten, made. “Before the hills was I brought forth”: before those things, I was made first.

“When he prepared the heavens, I was there.” “When he appointed the foundations of the earth: Then I was by him, as one brought up with him”: he gave Christ these commandments and Christ fulfilled them. “And I was daily his delight, rejoicing always before him.” That is the Word that was with God.

First the prologue: this Jesus was the son of Sirach and grandson of Jesus of the same name. The grandfather gathered the grave and short sentences of wise men before him and uttered some of his own, full of understanding and wisdom; the grandson compiled it into one volume and called it wisdom. It contains wise sayings, dark sentences and parables, and this Jesus imitated Solomon, repeating the things Solomon said, and was famous for wisdom as Solomon was.

“Wisdom shall praise herself, and shall glory in the midst of her people.” Solomon called wisdom a her, and Sirach repeats the same thing. “In the congregation of the most High shall she open her mouth.”

“I came out of the mouth of the most High.” Where did wisdom come from? Out of the mouth of the Most High. What is Christ called? The Word of God. So when the Father spoke, his Son was made. Christ is his Father’s Word. “And covered the earth as a cloud”: when the Father said something, his Son was doing it.

“I dwelt in high places, and my throne is in a cloudy pillar.” Christ has a throne. Some say Christ has no throne, standing in a corner on punishment; no, Christ has a throne. “I alone compassed the circuit of heaven, and walked in the bottom of the deep.”

Ecclesiasticus 24:6 says, “in every people and nation, I got a possession.” What does that mean? David saw in a vision what the Father promised the Son, and recites it. “Yet have I set my king upon my holy hill of Zion”: the I is the Father.

“I will declare the decree: the Lord hath said unto me”: this is Christ speaking through David, telling us what his Father said to him. “Thou art my Son; this day have I begotten thee.” This day: his beginning. Now you are my Son; this day I made you.

“Ask of me, and I shall give thee the heathen for thine inheritance, and the uttermost parts of the earth for thy possession.” The moment the Father made the Son, he said the nations are going to be yours; you will inherit everything because you are my Son. What does that prove? Christ has a beginning.

“In the waves of the sea and in all the earth, and in every people and nation, I got a possession.” He inherited the nations. When the Father made the Son he said, you are my Son, this day have I begotten thee, and when I make those nations you will inherit them and they will belong to you. Before they were made, they already belonged to him.

“With all these I sought rest”: after he was made and promised this inheritance, after he finished making everything, he sought rest. That is the Sabbath. “And in whose inheritance shall I abide?”

“So the Creator of all things gave me a commandment, and he that made me”: he that made me. Why are you confused? “Caused my tabernacle to rest.” Do Gods take naps? It is not talking about that. “And said, Let thy dwelling be in Jacob, and thine inheritance in Israel.” It tells you where the rest is: in a body. But it didn’t start with Jacob. It started well before that, with let us make man in our image.

sense.text: “Thou spakest at the beginning, when thou didst plant the earth, and that thyself alone, and commandedst the people.” What people did he command, and who was around at that time? That comes later in the class.

“And gavest a body unto Adam without soul.” He formed Adam, but Adam had no soul yet: he molded the clay and said, sit right there, I’ll put something in you later. “Which was the workmanship of thine hands”: Christ molded him; Christ made him.

“And didst breathe into him the breath of life”: the Father breathed into Adam the breath of life, “and he was made living before thee”, and then his body was activated. What, or rather who, is the breath of life? The precepts show it is Christ. The Son created the body, and that eternal spirit from the beginning in Proverbs 8 was put in that body by the Father. That is the rest he got.

It is like the movie Avatar, where they lie down and go into the body, or the Matrix, being plugged in. Before the earthly body he had a celestial body. Even that is very hard for everybody to understand, but those who are wise will understand it.

“He was made living before thee”: the thee is his Father. “And thou leadest him into paradise”: he formed Adam from the dust of the ground outside of paradise, then led him in. “Which thy right hand had planted”, which Christ made, “before ever the earth came forward.” So paradise was made before the earth was made.

Paradise is Christ’s throne, the cloudy pillar of his throne. He walked Adam into his own throne. And paradise is called rest; that is the rest it means when it says God rested.

precepts.why: To see what was breathed into Adam: “and the breath came into them, and they lived, and stood up upon their feet, an exceeding great army.” The breath entered into them and they lived, just like Adam.

“And after three days and an half the Spirit of life from God entered into them, and they stood upon their feet.” What Ezekiel called the breath, John calls the Spirit of life. The breath of life and the Spirit of life are the same thing, and it is from God.

Who is that Spirit of life, that breath of life? “Now the Lord is that Spirit: and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty.” The Spirit of life is Christ. So what was breathed into Adam? Christ. That is the rest right there.

“For wisdom is more moving than any motion: she passeth and goeth through all things by reason of her pureness.” They will say it says her, and Christ is a man; remember Solomon wrote Proverbs, and that is dealt with later.

“For she is the breath of the power of God”: wisdom is the breath and the power of God that was breathed into Adam, “and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty: therefore can no defiled thing fall into her.”

“For she is the brightness of the everlasting light, the unspotted mirror of the power of God, and the image of his goodness.” Keep that in mind: brightness and image.

“God, who at sundry times and in divers manners spake in time past unto the fathers by the prophets, Hath in these last days spoken unto us by his Son, whom he hath appointed heir of all things”: heir of all things, as in Psalms 2, where he inherits the nations. “By whom also he made the worlds”: he used his Son to make the worlds, the planets.

“Who being the brightness of his glory”: Solomon said wisdom is the brightness, the same thing. “And the express image of his person”: that is what wisdom is, the image of his goodness. Christ looks exactly like his Father.

“When he had by himself purged our sins, sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high.” Sat down. Not stood in the corner on punishment, not standing the whole time with no throne while his Father has a throne. He sat down on the right hand of his Father.

“And being but one, she can do all things: and remaining in herself, she maketh all things new: and in all ages entering into holy souls, she maketh them friends of God, and prophets.” In all ages she enters into holy souls. Who else does that?

“Even the Spirit of truth”: that same breath, “whom the world cannot receive, because it seeth him not, neither knoweth him: but ye know him; for he dwelleth with you, and shall be in you.” Entering into holy souls, and dwelling in you: that dwelling is a tabernacle.

“For we that are in this tabernacle do groan.” This tabernacle is the body we are in. “Being burdened: not for that we would be unclothed, but clothed upon, that mortality might be swallowed up of life”: clothed with an immortal body. Flesh and blood shall not inherit the kingdom of God; we will be clothed with a new body.

“As long as I am in this tabernacle, to stir you up by putting you in remembrance; Knowing that shortly I must put off this my tabernacle, even as our Lord Jesus Christ hath shewed me.” If he is taking that tabernacle off, he is putting on the new one, and Christ showed him that. His tabernacle is his earthly body.

“For the thoughts of mortal men are miserable, and our devices are but uncertain. For the corruptible body presseth down the soul”: the corruptible body is this earthy, fleshly, sinful tabernacle we are in, “and the earthy tabernacle weigheth down the mind that museth upon many things.”

Solomon calls it the earthy tabernacle. Peter called it a tabernacle, Paul called it a tabernacle, Solomon called it a tabernacle. The body is the tabernacle wisdom rests in.

“And the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life.” The Father used his Son to make everything, and then breathed into Adam the breath of life. Who was the breath of life? Christ. That is what the rest is. “And man became a living soul”: Adam was activated.

Christ created everything; the Lord spoke it and he did it; and after he created everything the Father put him in a body, an earthly body. Before that he had a celestial body.

Solomon is speaking of a man making idols, but he gives a comparison of how we are made: “Forasmuch as he knew not his Maker, and him that inspired into him an active soul, and breathed in a living spirit.” An active soul: that is why Adam is said to have been activated. Before, Adam was just a body with no soul in it. Once the Father put Christ in there the body was animated: walking around, moving his hands, looking around. The Father breathed into Adam a living spirit, and that is Christ.

“And the Lord God planted a garden eastward in Eden.” Is that an actual garden with flowers and trees and roses? No. “And there he put the man whom he had formed”: he led him into paradise, the garden of God.

One verse clears up a whole lot: “For unto you is paradise opened, the tree of life is planted”: the tree of life is located in the garden, in paradise. “The time to come is prepared, plenteousness is made ready, a city is builded”: paradise is the city. “And rest is allowed, yea, perfect goodness and wisdom.”

So where was Adam? In rest: Christ resting from all his labors of making everything, resting in his throne that was on the earth at that time. But Adam was made of the earth, which was not perfect; it was fallible. So he couldn’t stay there long. It was temporary, because flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom.

The thief who repented on the cross was told, this day you will be with me in paradise. When the righteous die, that is where they go. Christ said come unto me, all ye that labour, and I will give you rest. Everyone who dies goes to the spiritual realm, but not to the same place; there are heights of heaven, levels, and the top floor is the holy of holies where the Father is.

Ezra was shown a vision of a woman mourning her son. “Behold, her face upon a sudden shined exceedingly, and her countenance glistered, so that I was afraid of her.” “And, behold, suddenly she made a great cry very fearful: so that the earth shook at the noise of the woman.” “The woman appeared unto me no more, but there was a city builded, and a large place shewed itself from the foundations.” She vanished and became a city: a building so massive he could see the foundations.

He was terrified and cried, “Where is Uriel the angel, who came unto me at the first?” “And, lo, I lay as one that had been dead”: Ezra fainted at what he saw. Uriel set him on his feet and asked, “What aileth thee?” “Because thou hast forsaken me”: you left me by myself to see this. “I have seen, and yet see, that I am not able to express.” It was beyond anything he had ever seen.

Then Uriel explains: “This woman, whom thou sawest is Sion.” Because Ezra grieved sincerely for his people, not for money and clout, he was shown “the brightness of her glory.” He was told to go into a field “where no foundation of any building was”, “For in the place wherein the Highest beginneth to shew his city, there can no man’s building be able to stand.” No temple men build will be standing when the Father’s building shows up here.

“Go thy way in, and see the beauty and greatness of the building”: Uriel told Ezra to come inside. “For thou art blessed above many other, and art called with the Highest; and so are but few”, the same thing Christ said about John. That is the fourth temple Bishop went over the week before: access to the Father. It is already up there.

The Lord walked Adam into paradise, and paradise was on earth. “Behold, the time shall come, that these tokens which I have told thee shall come to pass, and the bride shall appear, and she coming forth shall be seen, that now is withdrawn from the earth.”

What was withdrawn from the earth? Paradise. When? When Adam fell. That caused a lot of death. Then at the end of the Bible it is brought back on the earth, to its rightful owner, and the same one who was cast out of it is put back in it with his children.

“And I saw a new heaven and a new earth: for the first heaven and the first earth were passed away; and there was no more sea”: no more Edom, no more nations. “And I John saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.”

What was withdrawn from the earth will be put back on the earth. That is the bride, the woman Ezra saw. When we pray thy kingdom come, thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven, that is what we are praying for: that fourth temple. As it is up there, with the angels, it will be on the earth, and the nations won’t be there. You are praying for the nations to be gone, not for them to be saved. Those who are wise will get it; this is your hope.

sense.text: The Christians and the apologetics say wisdom is a she, so that is not Christ. “So the Creator of all things gave me a commandment, and he that made me caused my tabernacle to rest.” Where did his body rest the first time? In Adam. “And said, Let thy dwelling be in Jacob, and thine inheritance in Israel”, because out of Adam came Israel.

“He created me from the beginning before the world, and I shall never fail.” He created me, from the beginning, before the world; and then I made the world. Wisdom is Christ there.

Read with verse 1, “Wisdom shall praise herself, and shall glory in the midst of her people”: wisdom has a people, an ethnicity. It is referring to someone, not something.

“In the holy tabernacle I served before him.” Past tense. Where is that? In Adam, but before that, upstairs: in the heavens where the Father is, the upper room. He served before him up there. “And so was I established in Sion”: when he served him again in Zion.

precepts.why: Who was wisdom? “Why speakest thou unto them in parables?” “Because it is given unto you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it is not given.” Christ spoke in parables because he was dealing with a selective audience: he spoke in parables, but revealed it to his children.

Remember Solomon wrote Proverbs. “These things have I spoken unto you in proverbs”, and the margin gives parables. So a proverb is a parable, and Solomon wrote Proverbs. That would explain why wisdom is called a she.

“But the time cometh, when I shall no more speak unto you in proverbs, but I shall shew you plainly of the Father.” And he does, later on.

So there are parables, proverbs, and the dark sentences read in the prologue of Ecclesiasticus. “Give ear, O my people, to my law”: “I will open my mouth in a parable: I will utter dark sayings of old.” Asaph says he will utter dark sayings of old: things written by Moses and the prophets before him.

“Which we have heard and known, and our fathers have told us.” What did our fathers tell us? The words of Moses and the prophets. Moses spoke dark sentences and sayings before David, before Asaph. Their fathers were not quoting David, who wasn’t born yet; they were quoting the dark sayings the prophets got from Moses.

Where did our fathers get dark sayings from? “In the bush I did manifestly reveal myself unto Moses, and talked with him, when my people served in Egypt.” He brought him up the mount and held him a long season, forty days and forty nights, “And told him many wondrous things, and shewed him the secrets of the times, and the end”: the beginning of time, the middle of time and the end of times, the end of everything, Christ’s return.

“These words shalt thou declare”: the commandments, the law, the statutes, made plain and public. “And these shalt thou hide”: some sayings hidden from those who should not know them, dark to some, that only the elect will read and say, wait a minute, there is more to this than thou shalt not steal. There are darker layers to the law: don’t mingle your seed, wearing fringes, sacrificing an animal and sprinkling the blood on the altar, which is the Messiah. Layers: dark sayings, sentences, parables, proverbs.

“I have also spoken by the prophets, and I have multiplied visions, and used similitudes, by the ministry of the prophets.” The prophets also spoke in parables, proverbs, dark sayings and similitudes: an illustrated story that means something else, or something more.

“If a man desire much experience, she knoweth things of old, and conjectureth aright what is to come”: she can determine from what the Bible says what is to come, correctly, not making things up like nations being saved. “She knoweth the subtilties of speeches”: when Moses or Isaiah or Jeremiah says one thing, he means something more. There are layers to the secrets.

“And can expound dark sentences.” Dark sentences, parables, proverbs, dark sayings, things to hide, similitudes: we keep finding them. And wisdom is what teaches these things.

What is wisdom? “Behold, I have taught you statutes and judgments, even as the Lord my God commanded me.” “Keep therefore and do them; for this is your wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the nations, which shall hear all these statutes, and say, Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people.”

The laws of God, the commandments of God, are our wisdom, given under the covenant with Moses. So wisdom and the commandments or laws are interchangeable; they are the same thing.

“The covenant, that was confirmed before of God in Christ, the law, which was four hundred and thirty years after, cannot disannul.” So the covenant and the law are synonymous: covenant, law, wisdom. (In that context the law is the sacrifices, but the point here is that law and covenant are one word.)

“Tell me, ye that desire to be under the law, do ye not hear the law? For it is written, that Abraham had two sons, the one by a bondmaid, the other by a freewoman.” That history is in Genesis; that is the law. The bondwoman is Hagar, mother of Ishmael: “he who was of the bondwoman was born after the flesh.” That child was not promised; he was a child of desperation, of their own carnal desire for an heir. “But he of the freewoman was by promise”: Isaac, promised to Sarah in her old age.

“Which things are an allegory.” Another word for allegory is parable, proverb, dark saying, similitude: the Old Testament has layers. “For these are the two covenants; the one from the mount Sinai, which gendereth to bondage, which is Agar.” Hagar is the old covenant, and Sarah the new. So the law, our wisdom, is called two women.

“For this Agar is mount Sinai in Arabia, and answereth to Jerusalem which now is”: there was a school in Arabia that answered to the one in Jerusalem and taught the old covenant. “But Jerusalem which is above is free, which is the mother of us all.”

“Cast out the bondwoman and her son: for the son of the bondwoman shall not be heir with the son of the freewoman.” You aren’t saving these nations; they can’t be heirs with us. “So then, brethren, we are not children of the bondwoman, but of the free.” Paul is writing to Israelites in Galatia. The law is called two women allegorically, and that is why a proverb calls wisdom a she.

Who wrote these proverbs and songs? “And he spake three thousand proverbs: and his songs were a thousand and five.” Solomon wrote the songs and the proverbs, not his women. We have just thirty-one chapters of them.
“The countries marvelled at thee for thy songs, and proverbs, and parables, and interpretations.” Solomon wrote songs and proverbs and parables, like the Song of Solomon, which is a parable.

Did Paul figure out who the wisdom Solomon wrote about is? “But unto them which are called, both Jews and Greeks”: the called of God are Israelites; the other nations were never called. “Christ the power of God, and the wisdom of God.”

What is Christ? The wisdom of God. So the wisdom we read about in Proverbs 8 that was created, and in Ecclesiasticus 24 that was created: that was Christ, allegorically.

Christ says in red letters: “Wherefore, behold, I send unto you prophets, and wise men, and scribes.” The scribes include Mark and Luke, who were not of the twelve; the prophets include the twelve and Paul. “And some of them ye shall kill and crucify.”

“That upon you may come all the righteous blood shed upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel unto the blood of Zacharias son of Barachias.” Christ says, I send.

The same words in Luke: “Therefore also said the wisdom of God, I will send them prophets and apostles.” What did Christ call himself? The wisdom of God. The wisdom of God is talking, saying what he will do. “That the blood of all the prophets, which was shed from the foundation of the world, may be required of this generation; From the blood of Abel unto the blood of Zacharias”, as in Matthew 23.

So when Solomon wrote that proverb of wisdom being a woman, it is the same thing Paul wrote of Hagar and Sarah, allegorically of the old covenant and the new. The wisdom of God in Proverbs 8, in Ecclesiasticus 24, in the Wisdom of Solomon, is Christ. Proverbs are parables.
“Then I was by him, as one brought up with him: and I was daily his delight, rejoicing always before him.” That is how he served before him in the holy tabernacle.

“We have such an high priest, who is set on the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens”: sitting down. “A minister of the sanctuary”: he is doing again what he did before. “And of the true tabernacle, which the Lord pitched, and not man.”

Where is that tabernacle now? Not on earth: in paradise, in heaven. That is where Christ serves him now. The same way he served the Father up there before, he does again since he left us. That is the fourth temple that withdrew itself, the city not built with hands, the real tabernacle Christ went into when he came before the Lord in Daniel 7.

sense.text: When the Father made his Son he said, this day have I begotten thee, and the Son gained the possession of nations and people. Now we are back with Adam. “And the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.”
“It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him”: a help suitable for him.
“Brought them unto Adam to see what he would call them: and whatsoever Adam called every living creature, that was the name thereof.” Adam had dominion and power on the earth to do that.

“But for Adam there was not found an help meet for him.” Adam was alone. The animals had mates, female birds and male birds, female bears and male bears; there was no mate for Adam, because he was the first. He was the first man ever made. There were no other people around; that doctrine is crazy.

It was taught years ago that there were other people around, but the understanding has been brought forth from the scriptures that Adam was in fact the first man, the first formed father of the world. That doesn’t mean nations can be saved; nothing changed there. Adam and Eve had many children, before he fell and after, and where Cain got his wife is one of those children who survived the destruction when paradise was withdrawn. Moses was told to hide some things.

“And the Lord God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam”: in this context, the Father. “And he took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh instead thereof”: he took the rib out of Adam and closed him up.

“And the rib, which the Lord God had taken from man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man.” This is the marriage. “This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man.” Woman means out of man.

Where did Eve come from? Out of Adam. Where was she before she was taken out of Adam? In Adam. This is very important, because there are layers to it. Keep it in mind: it comes back for Christ and his Father, and for Christ and Israel.

precepts.why: “For the first Adam”: the first Adam. There is only one. Orphans cause confusion. “Bearing a wicked heart transgressed, and was overcome; and so be all they that are born of him.” Why a wicked heart? He was made of the ground, the earth, which is corrupt. So Adam was fallible, and he couldn’t stay in paradise long.

“Upon the sixth day thou gavest commandment unto the earth, that before thee it should bring forth beasts, cattle, and creeping things: And after these, Adam also, whom thou madest lord of all thy creatures.” Adam was made on the sixth day. Don’t let anyone tell you different.

“Of him come we all, and the people also whom thou hast chosen.” Out of Adam came all people, and the people he chose. There were chosen people already around that came out of Adam first, Seth’s line, called the sons of God; then down the line came Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, called sons of God again. There was always a chosen people, even before there was an earth.

“She preserved the first formed father of the world.” So many layers in that verse alone. The first formed father of the world: who is that? Christ. Was he the first formed? Yes. “That was created alone”: was Christ created alone? Yes. And it is Adam too, the first formed father: of him came everyone on the earth, including the twelve tribes whom the Lord has chosen. Christ is the father of the world.

“And brought him out of his fall, And gave him power to rule all things”: temporarily; he will get that power when he returns.

To sum it up: “Which was the son of Enos, which was the son of Seth, which was the son of Adam, which was the son of God.” What was Adam? The son of God.

The first formed father of the world: he is literally our father in many layers, our father up there and our father down here. As it is in heaven, so on earth: our king up there, and he is going to be our king down here. And Christ is Adam. When you hear that Christ is the Son of God, that is what it means: he is Adam.

“These things saith the Amen, the faithful and true witness, the beginning of the creation of God.” It is the same thing as the first formed father: he is the beginning of the creation of God, the first thing the Father made. Celebrating Thanksgiving, celebrating murder and eating turkey, and talking about the trinity: we don’t teach that, and we don’t teach salvation to our oppressor either.

“Who is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature”: the first formed of every creature in heaven and on earth. “For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth”, including Adam, “visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him.”

“And he is before all things”: how? He is the first thing formed in heaven, and he is Adam, the first man formed on the earth. “And by him all things consist.” “And he is the head of the body, the church”, and that church is us, “who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead; that in all things he might have the preeminence.” He has preeminence over everything in heaven and on earth because he is the first formed in both: he is the father of everything, the everlasting Father. But not his own father; he is not the Ancient of days.

Three personalities in one guy is a schizophrenic god. If the Son and the Father are one all-knowing person, what do they talk about? You’re my Son; thank you, Father. It makes no sense.

sense.text:
“And being made perfect”: when he died. “He became the author of eternal salvation unto all them that obey him.” He is the author: from him is the beginning of our story, of our captivity in this Bible, and in him it comes to an end. He is the author of everything.

How do we get salvation today? We learn the Bible, and an author is the one who writes it. Lo, I come in the volume of the book, it is written of me: he is the author, the one written of all through the book.

precepts.why:
“Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God.” Set down, not standing.

What we read in the very beginning of the book, and the end of the book, is him. He is the writer of the story and the beginning of the story: the author, and the character in his own book. He wrote everything first and said, I am going to jump in this body and do all I wrote here. That is why the Bible is called the will of God: when a man writes a will, whatever is in it must be carried out after he is gone. I am going to come on the earth; I am going to be Adam; Israel will go off, go into captivity on ships, be scattered, lose their nationality, wake up again; I will jump back into them, bring them life again, and come save them. Him coming to save us is the end: that is the finisher. He is our creator, and the ender of our captivity, bringing us back where we were before.

Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end: the same thing. “The Revelation of Jesus Christ, which God gave unto him”: God gave Christ the revelation of what is going to happen. “To shew unto his servants things which must shortly come to pass.”

Who showed us the things that must come to pass, in Isaiah, Jeremiah, Daniel, Revelation? The author of our faith. Christ is the one who showed the prophets the things to come, and spoke to our forefathers all through the scriptures. That is the order.

sense.text: “Likewise in the beloved city he gave me rest”: there it is again. The beloved city is Jerusalem; now it is fast-forwarding. “And in Jerusalem was my power.” Who had power in Jerusalem and on earth at this time? Solomon.
“And I took root in an honourable people, even in the portion of the Lord’s inheritance.” That goes into Solomon, into David, into that line. Wisdom took root in that lineage.

“I was exalted like a cedar in Libanus, and as a cypress tree upon the mountains of Hermon.” He was exalted like a tree: a palm tree, a rose plant, a fair olive tree, a plane tree by the water, giving a sweet smell like cinnamon and myrrh and the fume of frankincense in the tabernacle. “As the turpentine tree I stretched out my branches, and my branches are the branches of honour and grace.” My branches: keep that in mind.
“As the vine brought I forth pleasant savour, and my flowers are the fruit of honour and riches.” Who is this vine?

precepts.why:
Someone will say, if Christ was Solomon, who did Solomon pray to? These gotcha moments are sad. “After this manner therefore pray ye: Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name.” When we pray, we pray to the Father. Christ is the way to the Father, so we have faith in Christ and pray through Christ to the Father. Solomon prays to the Father too.

All through the Old Testament our forefathers, except certain prophets, thought they were dealing with the Father, and they were dealing with Christ: Abraham, Moses, all of them. That is the hidden mystery. And there are other intermediaries, angels, who go to the Father on our behalf. You don’t go directly to the Father; there is an order, a hierarchy, a godhead.

“I am the true vine”: he is the root of us all, from Adam all the way down to now. “And my Father is the husbandman”: the Father planted him in the earth.

“I am the vine, ye are the branches”, as wisdom said in Ecclesiasticus 24. Those he is talking to are the branches that come out of the vine. Remember Eve: where was she before she was taken out of Adam? Part of Adam.

“Son of man”: God called Ezekiel son of man, and Christ son of man. What did Christ have that Ezekiel had? A daddy. “Speak unto Pharaoh king of Egypt, and to his multitude; Whom art thou like in thy greatness?” The Lord is showing Ezekiel who Assyria and Egypt are like in their glory.

“Behold, the Assyrian was a cedar in Lebanon with fair branches”: wisdom said in Ecclesiasticus 24, I was exalted like a cedar. A huge tree, shadowing all the others. “The waters made him great”: the waters are understanding, nourishing him. “His height was exalted above all the trees of the field, and his boughs were multiplied, and his branches became long because of the multitude of waters”: because of the wisdom he had, like Solomon.

“All the fowls of heaven made their nests in his boughs”: they sat down and learned from him. The same way people sought Solomon for wisdom, they sought Adam. “And under his shadow dwelt all great nations”: there were nations then too, with Adam, and a chosen people even then. “For his root was by great waters”: much wisdom. You can’t rule all things without wisdom.

“The cedars in the garden of God could not hide him”: the garden of God is paradise. “Nor any tree in the garden of God was like unto him in his beauty.” “So that all the trees of Eden, that were in the garden of God, envied him”, because Adam was the one to go to. He ruled everything; he was lord of everything. Adam’s history is completely parallel to Solomon’s. Who did Adam fall victim to, and who did Solomon fall victim to? Who ruled in paradise, and who ruled in Jerusalem?

An example of what the tree and the waters mean: “Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly”, “But his delight is in the law of the Lord; and in his law doth he meditate day and night. And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season”: righteousness. When he meditates on God’s laws and commandments, he is like a tree planted by water. So the water is God’s commandments, his laws, his wisdom.

“The sceptre shall not depart from Judah”: rulership. “Nor a lawgiver from between his feet”: this goes back into Adam. It is heavy, layers to the scriptures: there were tribes in the beginning.

“Until Shiloh come; and unto him shall the gathering of the people be.” Shiloh and Solomon mean the same thing: the peaceable one. When Solomon ruled, his kingdom was peaceful; peace was set up for Israel. Christ is Shiloh too, and when Christ returns there will be peace for our people the same way. It is twofold.

“Hear ye this, O house of Jacob, which are called by the name of Israel, and are come forth out of the waters of Judah.” Out of the waters of Judah: that is what Adam was before. That tribe has always been around. The scripture says restore thy judges as at the first; the city coming down from God in Revelation, already prepared, has twelve gates with the twelve tribes on them, showing the twelve tribes were there in the beginning. Moses was told to hide some things, so in Genesis 6 instead of the twelve tribes he wrote the sons of God. Abraham was Judah.

“The portion of Jacob is not like them: for he is the former of all things; and Israel is the rod of his inheritance: The Lord of hosts is his name.” The portion of Jacob is Christ, the former of all things. Israel has been around since the very, very beginning.

“And thou shalt say unto Pharaoh, Thus saith the Lord, Israel is my son, even my firstborn.” Israel was before all nations. We are the firstborn: we were the first created, and that means we get the inheritance, the same way Christ was the first created.

The scripture also shows we were the last nation formed and put in a land. The first shall be last and the last shall be first: we were the last nation, but the first people created.

sense.text:
“That the God of our Lord Jesus Christ”: Christ is our Lord. “The Father of glory, may give unto you the spirit of wisdom and revelation in the knowledge of him.” To understand the knowledge of Christ, the Lord has to give it to you. Christ told Peter, flesh and blood did not reveal it unto thee, but my Father. There is no way to understand the Bible, or who Christ really is, unless God gives it to you.

In the time of the Pharisees and the scribes they couldn’t understand; they were blinded. In the time of the apostles the argument was that Christ was the God that created everything, the God who was with Moses speaking to him, and the Pharisees and Sadducees couldn’t see it. Peter and the elect, the people God called, saw the mystery in Christ.

When it was read again later in the class: “That the God of our Lord”. The God of our Lord Jesus Christ. Keep that in mind; it is important.

“The eyes of your understanding being enlightened; that ye may know what is the hope of his calling.” What is the hope? You keep the commandments, you are not committing adultery, not lying, not stealing, you keep the Sabbath: why are we doing what we are doing? “And what the riches of the glory of his inheritance in the saints.” The riches prepared for us, touched on earlier with the kingdom of heaven, are on another level.
“And what is the exceeding greatness of his power to us-ward who believe.” What we are to see is that this was hidden from us, and it has to be given.

precepts.why: “And without controversy great is the mystery of godliness: God was manifest in the flesh, justified in the Spirit, seen of angels, preached unto the Gentiles, believed on in the world, received up into glory.” That is the mystery the God of our Lord gives the knowledge of.

“And wisdom was with thee: which knoweth thy works, and was present when thou madest the world.” Wisdom was present when God made the world. That goes back to John 1:1, the Word that was with God, and let us make man in our image. “And knew what was acceptable in thy sight, and right in thy commandments.”

“O send her out of thy holy heavens, and from the throne of thy glory, that being present she may labour with me, that I may know what is pleasing unto thee. For she knoweth and understandeth all things”: things we don’t. “And she shall lead me soberly in my doings, and preserve me in her power.” All of that is talking about Christ: the spirit of wisdom the Father gives.

sense.text:
“I am the mother of fair love, and fear, and knowledge, and holy hope: I therefore, being eternal”: Christ is eternal, but he is not the Ancient of days. “Am given to all my children which are named of him.”

Given to all my children which are named of whom? Of him: the Father named Christ’s children. The Father handpicked which ones are Christ’s children and which are not. Those are the twelve and those who hear the twelve. The other nations are not his children.

precepts.why: “I am the vine, ye are the branches: He that abideth in me, and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit: for without me ye can do nothing.” Christ said I am the vine: that goes back to Ecclesiasticus 24:17, where wisdom is the vine. Wisdom is divine; that is Christ there.

For the trinitarians: “And this is life eternal, that they might know thee the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom thou hast sent.” The only true God is his Father. And Jesus Christ, whom thou hast sent.

The verse they twist and corrupt, read slowly: “And we know that the Son of God is come”: he came, died and resurrected. “And hath given us an understanding, that we may know him that is true”: focus on the him. “And we are in him that is true, even in his Son Jesus Christ.” Who is the him whose Son is Jesus Christ? The Father.

“This is the true God, and eternal life.” Who is the true God? The Father, as Christ said in John 17:3. Christ is a God, but he is not the true God; Christ is the true witness of that true God.

“And now, O Father, glorify thou me with thine own self with the glory which I had with thee before the world was.” Christ had a glory before the world was created, which was lost and regained.

Verse 8: “And have known surely that I came out from thee.” Where did Eve come from? Out of Adam; woman means out of man. Where did Christ come from? Out of his Father. It parallels. Christ is not his Father’s wife; it is the same parallel: as Christ came out of his Father and they are one, Eve came out of Adam and they are one, yet two separate entities. The trinity is garbage.

Verse 20: “Neither pray I for these alone, but for them also which shall believe on me through their word”: not the twelve alone, but all the Israelites who believe what they teach. “That they all may be one; as thou, Father, art in me, and I in thee, that they also may be one in us.” Millions of us, all one: one in the sense of having the same spirit, not one entity. That is why Christ said I and my Father are one: they are in one accord, the way Adam and Eve are one.

“And the glory which thou gavest me I have given them”: we get the same, because we had it before the world was. “Father, I will that they also, whom thou hast given me”: the Father named them, as Ecclesiasticus 24:18 says. These are yours; those I am going to destroy. That is why when Christ said follow me, they followed: they had followed him before. A child knows his parent’s voice. “Be with me where I am”: when paradise comes down here, his children will be with him. “That the love wherewith thou hast loved me may be in them, and I in them”: wisdom entering into holy souls, the same as Wisdom of Solomon 7:27.

Where were his children? “And now when I prepared the world, which was not yet made, even for them to dwell in that now live, no man spake against me. For then every one obeyed”: all his children obeyed him at that time. “But now the manners of them which are created in this world that is made are corrupted by a perpetual seed”: by this earth. The earthly tabernacle made us corrupt, and we reject. In the heavens, in the beginning, we were obedient, because we were in our bodies there, always with the Son.
“But wisdom is justified of all her children.” Wisdom is received, taught and understood by all her children. Wisdom, which is Christ, and her children, named of the Father.

sense.text:
“Being made so much better than the angels”: being made. Creation again. “As he hath by inheritance obtained a more excellent name than they.” Why more excellent? Because he was first, the first formed.

When a father has a son, who is the son named after? The son takes on the father’s name, as on earth so in heaven. For the most part the Son retains the same titles the Father has. So when you read the capital LORD you can’t say that is always the Father.

“For unto which of the angels said he at any time, Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee?” That is Psalms 2. None of them, because the first thing the Father formed was Christ.

“And again, I will be to him a Father, and he shall be to me a Son?” Now Paul is pulling precepts: from the Psalms he runs to 2 Samuel. That is line upon line, rightly dividing; no Strong’s, no concordance, no commentary.

“And again, when he bringeth in the firstbegotten into the world”: when Christ came into the world and died for us. “He saith, And let all the angels of God worship him.” When he died, resurrected, and returned to the heavens in Acts 1, the angels of God went up there and worshipped him.
“Who maketh his angels spirits, and his ministers a flame of fire.” The angels are ministers that serve the Lord.

“But unto the Son he saith, Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever.” He is telling you who it is: the Son, O God. “Therefore God, even thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.” Fellows means the angels above and us as well: he is the head of the corner, the headstone.

“And, Thou, Lord, in the beginning hast laid the foundation of the earth; and the heavens are the works of thine hands.” In the beginning, thou Lord: that is Christ. “But thou art the same, and thy years shall not fail.” Wisdom said, I shall never fail.
“But to which of the angels said he at any time, Sit on my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool?” None, because none of them is called his son.
“Are they not all ministering spirits, sent forth to minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation?” Who are the heirs of salvation? We are. The angels are sent forth to minister unto us.

precepts.why:
Who is the Lord talking about? “When thy days be fulfilled, and thou shalt sleep with thy fathers”: David. “I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels”: Solomon, out of his loins. “He shall build an house for my name”: Solomon did. “And I will stablish the throne of his kingdom for ever”: Solomon didn’t last forever.

“I will be his father, and he shall be my son.” The Father is going to be the father of David’s son. “If he commit iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men, and with the stripes of the children of men.” Was Solomon chastened with the rod of men? No; he died old, and no one chastened him. So who is the Lord talking about? Christ. And Hebrews applies this very verse to the Son. So what is being revealed here about Solomon? Figure it out.
“And all such things as are either secret or manifest, them I know.” Solomon knew certain things, secret and manifest. Keep it in mind for his next words.

“For I was a witty child, and had a good spirit. Yea rather, being good, I came into a body undefiled.” Was Solomon’s body defiled? Yes, it was. Was Christ’s body defiled? No. Solomon knew who he was: he came back again. Things secret, I know, and things manifest, I know.

Now we have a clear understanding why the Lord said, I will be to him a Father, and he shall be to me a Son, and who Solomon was praying to, for the scoffers and their gotcha moments.

When the angels worshipped him: “a door was opened in heaven”, “Come up hither, and I will shew thee things which must be hereafter. And immediately I was in the spirit: and, behold, a throne was set in heaven, and one sat on the throne. And he that sat was to look upon like a jasper and a sardine stone”: a big brown man in heaven. “And there was a rainbow round about the throne, in sight like unto an emerald”: a green throne, and color in heaven; it isn’t black and white like an old cartoon.

“And round about the throne were four and twenty seats: and upon the seats I saw four and twenty elders sitting, clothed in white raiment; and they had on their heads crowns of gold.” With crowns of gold, they were kings, sitting on thrones. Christ is King of kings and Lord of lords: twenty-four elders have seats, and Christ has no seat, standing on the bench all day? What is wrong with these people?

“And out of the throne proceeded lightnings and thunderings and voices”: the same things heard at mount Sinai in Exodus. “Seven lamps of fire burning before the throne, which are the seven Spirits of God”: seven more angels standing before the throne, because the throne is huge. “A sea of glass like unto crystal”: the movies call it the Bifrost. Esau knows and puts it in the movies: a big black man sitting on a throne like Galactus, a black angel guarding the bridge who sees everything. The angels have eyes all over because they see everything on the earth.

“And round about the throne, were four beasts full of eyes before and behind”: four angels at the four sides of the throne, the faces of a lion, a calf, a man and an eagle; Ezekiel saw them with all four faces at once, so they don’t need to turn. Marvel calls it the Living Tribunal, the one that answers to the One Above All. That is called the godhead: there is order and structure up there. You don’t just go to the Father.

The four horns on the altar represent those four beasts that deal with judgment and mercy. That is why the blood of the sin offering was put on the horns, and why a man fleeing for his life, like Joab, ran and took hold of the horn of the altar.

“Six wings about him”; “they rest not day and night, saying, Holy, holy, holy, Lord God Almighty, which was, and is, and is to come”: that is the Father, who is to come when that paradise comes down here. “The four and twenty elders fall down before him that sat on the throne”, “and cast their crowns before the throne, saying, Thou art worthy, O Lord, to receive glory and honour and power: for thou hast created all things.”

“And I saw in the right hand of him that sat on the throne a book written within and on the backside, sealed with seven seals.” The Father sitting with a book in his right hand. “And I saw a strong angel proclaiming with a loud voice, Who is worthy to open the book”: the angel looked strong, but he couldn’t open it. “And no man in heaven, nor in earth, neither under the earth, was able to open the book”: no angel, none of the spirits who had passed on. “And I wept much.”

“Weep not: behold, the Lion of the tribe of Juda, the Root of David, hath prevailed to open the book.” Everyone is crying, and here comes Christ walking through, black, with a dramatic entrance. “Stood a Lamb as it had been slain”: this is after he died and came back in Acts 1. “Having seven horns and seven eyes, which are the seven Spirits of God sent forth into all the earth”: Christ has a crew, the seven angels, the watchers, war angels who regulate the earth and hold back the four winds. “And he came and took the book out of the right hand of him that sat upon the throne.”

“The four beasts and four and twenty elders fell down before the Lamb.” “Thou art worthy to take the book, and to open the seals thereof: for thou wast slain”: he came down, did no sin, was killed and was not overcome, and was found worthy. “And hast redeemed us to God by thy blood out of every kindred, and tongue, and people, and nation”: out of the sea, the nations we are scattered among. “And hast made us unto our God kings and priests: and we shall reign on the earth.” Everything is possessive: the Israelites and their God. They are going to bring heaven here.

“Ten thousand times ten thousand, and thousands of thousands”: millions of angels, our brothers up there. “Worthy is the Lamb that was slain to receive power”: the power he had before the world was, as in John 17, and his children get that glory too. “Be unto him that sitteth upon the throne, and unto the Lamb for ever and ever”: two separate entities. Christ is worshipped, and so is his Father.

Back to let all the angels worship him. “And the four and twenty elders, which sat before God on their seats.” They had seats, thrones, not benches. If they have thrones, who else has a throne? If there are two thrones, how many gods are there?

Christ is a God. Angels are gods. But there is one true God: the law says the Lord our God is one Lord, and that is true. That God is the God of our God, who is Christ, and we are the sons of God. There is a hierarchy, an order: the heavenly Father made his Son, and his Son made us. One true God that rules over other gods. We are not polytheists.

“The like figure whereunto even baptism doth also now save us (not the putting away of the filth of the flesh”: not water, “but the answer of a good conscience toward God,)”: keeping God’s laws, “by the resurrection of Jesus Christ: Who is gone into heaven, and is on the right hand of God; angels and authorities and powers being made subject unto him.” Being subject unto him, worshipping him, as Hebrews 1:6 says.

Why? Because he was found worthy to open the book and loose the seals that enable him to return and get us out of here. That book of seals opening is history unfolding as we speak: the end of our captivity, nations coming into existence, the world coming to an end, nuclear bombs being made, technology increasing, us waking up. Once the book was opened, everything in it could activate. That is why he is the author and finisher of our faith, Alpha and Omega, a title he shares with his Father: the Father is the beginning of all things, and through his Son he ends them.

“To him that overcometh will I grant to sit with me in my throne, even as I also overcame”: he was slain and overcame, “and am set down with my Father in his throne.” He is sat down with his Father in his throne, along with the twenty-four elders round about the Father. And they say he is just standing, on punishment, the whole time. Where do these doctrines come from?

“Who being the brightness of his glory, and the express image of his person”: he looks like his Father. “When he had by himself purged our sins, sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high.” Sat down, on the throne. The Majesty on high is the Father; he sat down on the right hand, next to his Father. If dad gets a throne, son gets a throne.

Read slow: “The Lord said unto my Lord.” Remember Ephesians 1:17, Jesus Christ our Lord. Why keep emphasizing that Christ is our Lord? Where was Eve before she was made? In Adam. And what is the man to the woman? The head. What did women call their men back then? Lord. Who is David’s Lord here?

“Sit thou at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool.” Are Christ’s enemies his footstool yet? No. So what is he doing now? Sitting and waiting until the Father tells him to come down. They are two separate entities: why would he sit and wait for himself, until he makes his own enemies his footstool? You would have to be high to say something that stupid. Wisdom is too high for a fool.

You can’t understand the divinity of Christ if you don’t understand the simple things about Christ. If they can’t tell you their nationality, don’t let them ask you about God’s divinity.

“What think ye of Christ? whose son is he? They say unto him, The Son of David.” “How then doth David in spirit call him Lord, saying, The Lord said unto my Lord, Sit thou on my right hand, till I make thine enemies thy footstool? If David then call him Lord, how is he his son?” Shouldn’t the son be calling the father Lord? Why is David calling his son Lord?

This was touched on in 2 Samuel 7: Nathan told David his son would be called the son of the Most High. David’s son was his Lord. And if Solomon was David’s Lord, then Solomon was the Messiah, Christ: that is what Solomon said, I came into a body undefiled, things secret and manifest I know. “And no man was able to answer him a word, neither durst any man from that day forth ask him any more questions.” If you receive it, you receive it.

“Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever”: was David’s throne forever? No. “The sceptre of thy kingdom is a right sceptre”: remember Genesis 49, the sceptre shall not depart from Judah.

“Thou lovest righteousness, and hatest wickedness: therefore God, thy God.” Who is God’s God? For the trinitarians: if Christ is his own father, then God the Father has another God he answers to. The Father is Christ’s God. “Hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows”: Christ has the preeminence, because he is the Son. Going back to the Psalms: the Lord said unto my Lord.

Therefore God, thy God: “I called upon the Lord, the Father of my Lord, that he would not leave me in the days of my trouble.” The Father of my Lord. That is who Solomon called upon too: the Father. Who is the thy God? Your Father.

sense.text: “For it became him, for whom are all things, and by whom are all things”: that is John 1:3. “In bringing many sons unto glory”: bringing his own children the same glory he had in the beginning, before the world was. “To make the captain of their salvation perfect through sufferings”: he is our captain of salvation.

“For both he that sanctifieth and they who are sanctified are all of one”: we are all of the Father, all connected, as in John 17. “For which cause he is not ashamed to call them brethren.” Why does he call his sons brethren? Two reasons. He created us, so he is our father. And he put himself into the loins of David. So he is not only the root of David, the father of David; he is also the offspring of David, the son of David. He created David and came out of David, as Solomon. That is heavy.

“I will declare thy name unto my brethren, in the midst of the church will I sing praise unto thee.” His brethren are called the church. That is who Christ is the head of: his brothers, his people. Not the Catholic church or the Pentecostal church.

“And again, I will put my trust in him. And again, Behold I and the children which God hath given me.” And again, and again: Paul is pulling from different precepts, line upon line, here quoting Isaiah 8:17-18. He calls them sons, then brethren, then children.

“Forasmuch then as the children are partakers of flesh and blood”: Christ’s children. How are children formed? Between a father and a mother. “He also himself likewise took part of the same”: he came into the world like everybody else, like his children. “That through death”, because he was immortal, “he might destroy him that had the power of death, that is, the devil”: the spiritual entity, and Edom as his children too. “And deliver them who through fear of death were all their lifetime subject to bondage”: which is us.
“For verily he took not on him the nature of angels”: he was not fully God and fully man; he was fully man. “But he took on him the seed of Abraham”: flesh and blood.

“Wherefore in all things it behoved him to be made like unto his brethren.” Put the emphasis on in all things: nothing changed in the way Christ was born on this earth. In all things he was made just like his brethren, and all his brethren were made through a father and a mother. “That he might be a merciful and faithful high priest in things pertaining to God, to make reconciliation for the sins of the people”: his own people.

precepts.why: I and the children which God hath given me: it was read earlier in Ecclesiasticus. “I therefore, being eternal, am given to all my children which are named of him.” All my children, named of the Father. The Father named them.

Hebrews is quoting what Isaiah said, but remember it is allegory, layers. “And I will wait upon the Lord, that hideth his face from the house of Jacob, and I will look for him. Behold, I and the children whom the Lord hath given me are for signs and for wonders in Israel.”

When Christ walked the earth he was a sign. When the disciples walked the earth, they were for signs. When the prophets walked the earth, Ezekiel, Hosea, Isaiah, they were used as signs. And they were God’s children.

sense.text:
“I Jesus have sent mine angel to testify unto you these things in the churches. I am the root and the offspring of David.” I am the root, the vine, and I am the offspring of David. That is why Christ asked the Pharisees, why does David call him Lord if he is his son? Because I am his father and I am his son at the same time. I formed David and I came out of David.

Why would he go through all of that? The law of the king shows why.

precepts.why:
