“When thou art come unto the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee”, “and shalt say, I will set a king over me, like as all the nations that are about me; Thou shalt in any wise set him king over thee, whom the Lord thy God shall choose: one from among thy brethren shalt thou set king over thee: thou mayest not set a stranger over thee.”

So the law says if we decide to set a king over ourselves like the nations, he must be of our own brethren. Normally we use this to say you can’t vote; Christ is our king. And this law was put there before Israel decided they wanted a king.

“Then all the elders of Israel gathered themselves together”, “And said unto him, Behold, thou art old, and thy sons walk not in thy ways”: Samuel’s sons went off. “Now make us a king to judge us like all the nations.” The law allowed it. “But the thing displeased Samuel.” Why would Samuel be displeased at something found in the law?

“For they have not rejected thee, but they have rejected me, that I should not reign over them.” So why was that law put there? Not every law is there for righteousness’ sake. Originally the Lord is already our king, and we were not supposed to ask for another king. The Lord knew that in the future we would reject him and desire a king over us. So he said, I’ve got you anyway: I will come through the loins of David and be your king anyway. You can’t reject me; my Father up there, and I will be down here with you. It was a law for those who did not want order over them.

Our government is a theocracy: God rule. Our king is a God. He came, and there was peace for forty years, and he set the people in order. And he made his home on earth: he replicated the heavens on earth while he reigned, from Adam on down, bringing heaven down to earth. That royal tribe always had access; that is why David wore a linen ephod.

sense.text: “For Zion’s sake will I not hold my peace, and for Jerusalem’s sake I will not rest, until the righteousness thereof go forth as brightness, and the salvation thereof as a lamp that burneth.”

“And the Gentiles shall see thy righteousness, and all kings thy glory”: the heathen. “And thou shalt be called by a new name.” Why? Because our Father will have a new name, and we will be called after his new name, because we are his children. “Which the mouth of the Lord shall name”: the mouth of the Father shall name it.
“Thou shalt also be a crown of glory in the hand of the Lord, and a royal diadem in the hand of thy God.” “For the Lord delighteth in thee, and thy land shall be married.”

“For as a young man marrieth a virgin, so shall thy sons marry thee.” Where was Eve before she was formed? So where were Christ’s children before they were formed, and where was Christ before he was formed?

The sons make up the nation, and the nation of Israel is the Lord’s wife, just as Eve was Adam’s wife. Christ is our Lord the same way Adam was Eve’s Lord. That parallels Ephesians 5.

“And as the bridegroom rejoiceth over the bride, so shall thy God rejoice over thee.” Christ is the bridegroom and we are the bride. That explains the ten virgins in Matthew 25: those virgins are Israelites. Not a man with multiple wives in captivity who can’t afford a chicken sandwich.

So not only is he our God, he is also our Lord, because the nation of Israel is his wife. He is our father, our brother, and our husband as a nation of people. Oh my God and my Lord.

precepts.why: “For I am jealous over you with godly jealousy: for I have espoused you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ.” One husband. That is the ten virgins: the nation presented as a chaste virgin to Christ.

Deeper now. “Behold, these heathen, which have ever been reputed as nothing”: the nations, all of them, good or bad, have always been reputed as nothing, insignificant. “Have begun to be lords over us, and to devour us.”

Read slow: “But we thy people, whom thou hast called thy firstborn.” He calls us his firstborn, because we are the first thing he formed. He is the firstborn of his Father; we are the firstborn of our Father. “Thy only begotten”: we are called Christ’s only begotten the same way he is his own Father’s only begotten. See the order. “And thy fervent lover”: that is us being his wife, his bride to be. His people, his firstborn, his only begotten, his fervent lover.

“Are given into their hands. If the world now be made for our sakes”: whatever was made, was made for us.

“For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him: And he is before all things, and by him all things consist.”

All things made by him were made for him, and for whom else? For us. Not by us, but for us: we share the same inheritance, because we are his children. We get the eternal inheritance promised to us before the world was made.

Now there is more clarity on what that firstborn means. The trinitarian says, if Christ is the firstborn you say he was made; what about David, who was called the firstborn though he was not his father’s firstborn child? Yes he was: he was the firstborn up there before he came down here.

“Thus saith the Lord, Israel is my son, even my firstborn.” That is literal, and that is Christ talking. The first thing he made was us, and everything else came after: then angels, then the devil, and everything else. We are the firstborn spiritually; as a nation we were the last. The first shall be last, and the last shall be first.

Concerning Christ being our father: after he died and resurrected, “Jesus stood on the shore: but the disciples knew not that it was Jesus”: he had his power back, so he changed his appearance. “Then Jesus saith unto them, Children, have ye any meat?” Why is Christ calling his disciples children? Because they are his children.

We are Christ’s sons; Christ created us. We are all children of Christ’s Father, but we are the firstborn, the ones given to Christ by the Father. We were with Christ in the beginning, ruling too; and when he fell, we fell.
“Then said he unto me, Even so also is Israel’s portion. Because for their sakes I made the world.” Before the world was made, he made the world for our sakes.

“The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God”: it is the spirit that bears witness with our spirit. “And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ.” Whatever the Father promised Christ, we get the same thing. The Father passes his inheritance on to his sons: in Psalms 2 he shall inherit the nations, and we inherit everything, heaven on earth, everything on earth and outside the earth. “If so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together.”

Verse 23: “Waiting for the adoption, to wit, the redemption of our body.” What is the adoption? Access to the Father, through Christ. Christ died on the cross and gave us access back to the Father. He is not only the only begotten Son any more; the adoption is for many sons he is bringing unto glory. That is why Christ tells us to pray, our Father. It is like Jacob taking Joseph’s sons as his own, to be part of the twelve.

An example of the adoption: “To him that overcometh will I grant to sit with me in my throne, even as I also overcame, and am set down with my Father in his throne.” That is what we are fighting to get: to overcome as he overcame. Our father is the firstfruits; he goes first, and we follow his steps to acquire the same thing he was worthy of: access to his Father, so we can have access to our Father. That is very hard; stick around and the understanding will come.

sense.text:
Read real slow: “For whom he did foreknow”: whom he knew before. “He also did predestinate.” Predestinate means destined before: decided or determined in advance, already fated or foreordained by a higher power. That was your lot from the beginning; that is your fate. King David was predestined: when he messed up the Lord said, I already forgave you, but I am going to bring evil on your house.

The Oracle in the Matrix told Neo, you didn’t come here to make the choice, you’ve already made it; you’re here to try to understand why you made it. Everyone in this room was called into this truth, had a void, and is figuring out who am I, what am I doing here. It is already written; we are living it out. The Oracle is the word, the Bible: it already knows whether you are going to be a defector and a traitor or the righteous protagonist. Your job is to play it out, and become the good guy or live long enough to see yourself become the villain. Over the Oracle’s door is written know thyself: examine yourself whether you be in the faith. Neo is called the one, and Christ said let them be one, even as we are one: we are the one.

Who did he foreknow? Israel. “To be conformed to the image of his Son”: overcoming the same way his Son did, walking the same steps. “That he might be the firstborn among many brethren”: not only the first begotten; many begotten.

The nation of Israel is predestined for the kingdom, but we don’t know who’s who. Many are called, few are chosen. You don’t know if you are chosen; the Lord knows them that are his. He that endureth to the end: when you die and wake up with the Lord, or when destruction comes and you are delivered up out of here, you know you are of the elect. You could be in this ten or twenty years and fall and not get up.

How you know it is not you: secretly in adultery or fornication and not trying to come out of it, carrying hatred for your brother or sister, disrespecting your spouse, sisters with a nasty disrespectful spirit toward their husbands. The elect, even if they fall, get back up. They make mistakes and fix them, try hard to do right by their people, love the Lord, and are into the scriptures. Some brothers can’t wait for the marathon class; some can’t wait for it to end so they can go home, or they are home with their wicked family smelling the turkey and the cranberry sauce.

“Moreover whom he did predestinate, them he also called”: both Jews and Greeks, whom he foreknew: Israelites. “And whom he called, them he also justified: and whom he justified, them he also glorified.” Precepts, please, not a concordance.

precepts.why: “Who are Israelites; to whom pertaineth the adoption”: the adoption, access to Christ’s Father, belongs only to the Israelites. “And the glory”: the rulership of this earth, living forever, pertains only to the Israelites. “And the covenants”: the first and the second belong only to the Israelites. “And the giving of the law”: the law was only given to the Israelites. “And the service of God”: the Israelites are God’s servants. “And the promises.” “Whose are the fathers.”

Christ is speaking to Thomas: “And whither I go ye know, and the way ye know.” Where I am going you know, and how to get there you already know, the same thing the Oracle told Neo. “Lord, we know not whither thou goest; and how can we know the way?”

“I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.” You get there through me, because I chose you. These men were predestined, already chosen, and Christ knew it. Predestination is real, but you can’t get puffed up and say I am chosen, I am the elect. None of us knows whether we are of the elect. And the other nations are not his children, no matter how good you think they are.

Who did God foreknow? “Hear this word that the Lord hath spoken against you, O children of Israel”: not all nations, not good nations. “Against the whole family which I brought up from the land of Egypt, saying, You only have I known of all the families of the earth.” So many layers: he knew us even before that. “Therefore I will punish you for all your iniquities”, because only us did he know from the very beginning.

Whom he called is whom he justified, both Jews and Greeks. Who is it? “In the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory.” Not all nations, not Israel and the good nations: all the seed of Israel, justified, and they shall glory: the same glory the Son had from the beginning. Romans 8:30 says them he justified and glorified, and Isaiah says the seed of Israel shall be justified and shall glory. Precept upon precept; no Hebrew and Greek needed.

sense.text:
“Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, to the saints which are at Ephesus, and to the faithful in Christ Jesus.” An apostle, not a false apostle. Who are the saints at Ephesus? The saints are the children of Israel.

Paul wrote to the Ephesians, a Greek colony, in the language they understood, and he defined saints from the Hebrew scriptures by precept. So why go to the Greek to define something we read in English? It makes no sense. Stop watching these kids; you will get yourselves confused and destroyed.

“Grace be to you, and peace, from God our Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ. Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.” Our Christ has a God. “Who hath blessed us with all spiritual blessings in heavenly places in Christ.”

“According as he hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world.” Chosen us where? In him. When? Before the foundation of the world. Before there was a world, we were already chosen in Christ. Where was Eve? In Adam. Where were we? In Christ. That is predestined, and it makes us the firstborn: when the Lord said, you are my firstborn, he was talking to us too. “That we should be holy and without blame before him in love.”

“Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself”: this is the Father. We become his children, the sons of God, through Christ: that is the adoption, to himself, to the Father. Christ is no longer the only begotten Son; we are all sons of God. That is why Christ teaches us to pray, our Father which art in heaven: he is my Father and he is your Father. For that, Christ had to come and die first.

Many things in the scriptures were hidden, a veil over everybody’s eyes, so that our people couldn’t see that Christ was the one dealing with us all through the scriptures. When he came and died, everything became clear.
“In whom also we have obtained an inheritance, being predestinated according to the purpose of him who worketh all things after the counsel of his own will.”

precepts.why: Who are the saints? “He also exalteth the horn of his people, the praise of all his saints; even of the children of Israel, a people near unto him.” His saints are his people, the children of Israel. Now we know who the saints at Ephesus are.

A sidebar for a question from the audience. “And I will make them one nation in the land upon the mountains of Israel; and one king shall be king to them all: and they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all.” That is Judah and Israel.

“Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea”, “in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God. Then shall the children of Judah and the children of Israel”: Judah and Ephraim, “be gathered together, and appoint themselves one head.”

“As the Father knoweth me, even so know I the Father: and I lay down my life for the sheep. And other sheep I have, which are not of this fold”: this fold is Judah. “Them also I must bring, and they shall hear my voice”: only his children hear his voice. “And there shall be one fold, and one shepherd”: one head, one king. That is Ezekiel 37:22. That is talking about Israel; stop with the nations.

“And not for that nation only”: Judah. “But that also he should gather together in one the children of God that were scattered abroad.” The other sheep: all twelve tribes. The other nations are not in there. You don’t put the pet in the same place as the master; the dog gets the dog house.

“Who hath saved us, and called us with an holy calling”: we are the called, and those who were predestinated are whom he called. “Not according to our works, but according to his own purpose and grace, which was given us in Christ Jesus before the world began.” The grace and mercy were given unto us in Christ before the world began, as Ephesians 1:4 says. We were always predestined to receive mercy and grace, before we were formed in the womb. That is why he told Jeremiah, before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee.

sense.text: “Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord.”
“For the husband is the head of the wife, even as Christ is the head of the church”: he is the bridegroom of the bride. “And he is the saviour of the body”: of his own body, us.

“Therefore as the church is subject unto Christ, so let the wives be to their own husbands in every thing.” The same relationship applies to us and Christ, and to wives and husbands. “Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it”: he died for his people, his wife. Adam died for Eve, pretty much.

“That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word”: teaching them the commandments. “That he might present it to himself a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle.” “For no man ever yet hated his own flesh; but nourisheth and cherisheth it, even as the Lord the church”, because we are the church of Acts 7:38.
“For we are members of his body, of his flesh, and of his bones.” Just like Eve was to Adam, we are members of his body. That is what it means that we were chosen in Christ: in his celestial body.
“And they two shall be one flesh. This is a great mystery: but I speak concerning Christ and the church.” Christ is the husband and the nation of Israel is the wife.

precepts.why: “This is he, that was in the church in the wilderness.” The church in the wilderness was the children of Israel; that is the church. “With the angel which spake to him in the mount Sina”: that is Christ. It says the angel spoke to Moses out of mount Sinai, not the Father. That is the voice they heard. “And with our fathers: who received the lively oracles to give unto us.”

sense.text: Now it is time to upset people. “For I am the Lord thy God, the Holy One of Israel, thy Saviour.” I am the Lord: the capital L-O-R-D, the tetragrammaton. The Holy One of Israel. Keep that title in mind. “I gave Egypt for thy ransom, Ethiopia and Seba for thee.”

“Ye are my witnesses, saith the Lord.” Not the Jehovah’s witnesses: we the Israelites are God’s witnesses. “That ye may know and believe me, and understand that I am he.” Keep those three words in mind: I am he.

“Before me there was no God formed, neither shall there be after me.” Before Christ there was no God formed, because he was the first formed. He is making it clear he was formed, and that no other God will be formed.

“I, even I, am the Lord; and beside me there is no saviour.” At that time Israel thought they could run to Egypt or hide from Assyria. The Lord said the only one that can save you is me; Egypt and Ethiopia won’t save you; you must rely on me alone.
“I am the Lord, your Holy One, the creator of Israel, your King.” Who is talking? They will say the Father, because of the capital LORD. That is why we do precepts here.

precepts.why:
Let’s see what the devils think. “A man with an unclean spirit; and he cried out, Saying, Let us alone; what have we to do with thee, thou Jesus of Nazareth? art thou come to destroy us? I know thee who thou art, the Holy One of God.” The demon knew him as the Holy One, the same one who told Isaiah he is the Holy One of Israel.

“And Jesus rebuked him, saying, Hold thy peace, and come out of him”: be quiet and get out, because he didn’t want anybody to know that.

“Therefore my heart is glad, and my glory rejoiceth: my flesh also shall rest in hope. For thou wilt not leave my soul in hell; neither wilt thou suffer thine Holy One to see corruption.” This is Christ speaking through David: you will not allow your Holy One to see corruption.

Peter quotes the same psalm: “For David speaketh concerning him, I foresaw the Lord always before my face, for he is on my right hand”, “Because thou wilt not leave my soul in hell, neither wilt thou suffer thine Holy One to see corruption.”

“Therefore being a prophet, and knowing that God had sworn with an oath to him, that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne; He seeing this before spake of the resurrection of Christ.” So David saw that the prophecy in Psalm 16 was of the Messiah: the Holy One of Israel is Christ.

“Thus saith the Lord, the Holy One of Israel, and his Maker.” The Holy One of Israel, and the Holy One of Israel’s Maker. “Ask me of things to come concerning my sons, and concerning the work of my hands command ye me.” That is Christ speaking, of himself and of his Maker.

Christ doesn’t speak on his own: what I say is not of myself, but of the Father who sent me. Christ speaks on behalf of his Father; everything he does is on behalf of his Father. When you see thus saith the Lord, it is Christ, or sometimes the angels, speaking on behalf of the Father, like an ambassador carrying a message. People hear it and think it is the Father speaking. No: the Father never spoke to anyone; no one ever heard his voice.

A precept for the Holy One of Israel and his Maker: “The Lord liveth; and blessed be my rock; and exalted be the God of the rock of my salvation.” Who is the rock? And who is the God of the rock? Thus saith the Holy One and his Maker; the rock and the God of the rock. The same exact thing.

“For thy Maker is thine husband”: we are married to him; he made us. Spiritually, of course. “The Lord of hosts is his name.” Is our maker the heavenly Father? Who made us? Christ. So who is the Lord of hosts here? They share that title. They share titles, except Ancient of days and Most High: that is not the Son at all. The Most High dwells above the heavens; that is the Father. The Ancient of days is older than days, older than time.

“And thy Redeemer the Holy One of Israel; The God of the whole earth shall he be called.”

Here is the Father: “For thus saith the high and lofty One that inhabiteth eternity.” He dwells outside of time; he is before time. “Whose name is Holy”, because we don’t know it. “I dwell in the high and holy place”: the holy tabernacle the elders sit in, the holy of holies above, that the temple was modeled after. “With him also that is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble.” The high and lofty One is not Christ at all; that is the heavenly Father.

“For every battle of the warrior is with confused noise, and garments rolled in blood”: regular warfare. “But this shall be with burning and fuel of fire”: nuclear war. “For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given”: given by the Father. “And the government shall be upon his shoulder”: Israel’s government. “And his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.”

His title is the mighty God. What is Christ called? The everlasting Father. Why? Because he is our maker, our father. “Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end, upon the throne of David”, “to establish it with judgment and with justice from henceforth even for ever.” The Son that is given to us is called the mighty God and the everlasting Father.

“I will raise unto David a righteous Branch”: branch, root, vine, stem, the same thing. “And a King shall reign and prosper, and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth”, as in Isaiah 9. “In his days Judah shall be saved, and Israel shall dwell safely: and this is his name whereby he shall be called, THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS.”

The king that comes out of David is called THE LORD. I thought that was the Father’s name? Did the Father come out of David’s line? No. You can’t guess who is who in the scripture by the capital letters. Just keep the commandments of God.

sense.text: Let’s make it worse. “In the year that king Uzziah died I saw also the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up, and his train filled the temple.” Isaiah saw the Lord sitting on the throne; here it is lower case, and they will say, see, that is Christ.

“Above it stood the seraphims: each one had six wings”: angels with six wings, as read in Revelation 4. One set covered the face, one the feet, and with the middle ones they flew. “And one cried unto another, and said, Holy, holy, holy, is the Lord of hosts: the whole earth is full of his glory.” This is the Lord Isaiah is seeing in his glory. “And the house was filled with smoke.”

“Woe is me! for I am undone; because I am a man of unclean lips, and I dwell in the midst of a people of unclean lips”: I am a wicked man among wicked people; why should I be allowed to see this? “For mine eyes have seen the King, the Lord of hosts.” The King, the Lord of hosts: the same title as in Jeremiah 23. So did Isaiah see the Father sitting there? It is in capitals, so they say it has to be the Father.
“Lo, this hath touched thy lips; and thine iniquity is taken away, and thy sin purged”: you are worthy to see what you have seen. Isaiah got a VIP pass.

“Also I heard the voice of the Lord”, the same Lord he saw sitting, the King, the Lord of hosts, “saying, Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” The us is the seraphims, the host of angels sitting there. “Then said I, Here am I; send me.”

“Hear ye indeed, but understand not; and see ye indeed, but perceive not. Make the heart of this people fat, and make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes; lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and convert, and be healed.” This is the Lord speaking to Isaiah after he saw him in his glory. Remember these words. Who did Isaiah see sitting on that throne?

precepts.why:
Let’s see who Isaiah saw. If anyone would know, it would be John, one of the twelve. “But though he had done so many miracles before them, yet they believed not on him”: Christ. “That the saying of Esaias the prophet might be fulfilled, which he spake, Lord, who hath believed our report? and to whom hath the arm of the Lord been revealed?” That is Isaiah 53:1.

“Therefore they could not believe, because that Esaias said again, He hath blinded their eyes, and hardened their heart; that they should not see with their eyes, nor understand with their heart, and be converted, and I should heal them”: the words of Isaiah 6:10.

“These things said Esaias, when he saw his glory, and spake of him.” Who did Isaiah see? Christ. So the Lord of hosts, the King in Isaiah 6, sitting there, is Christ. You can’t determine who is who by the capital L; stop that. Christ told the Pharisees none of them had ever heard the Father’s voice. It is always the angels or Christ speaking on behalf of the Father.

sense.text: Years ago on Clubhouse a brother was asked who this is, and he said the Father. Today that is answered. “Sanctify the Lord of hosts himself; and let him be your fear, and let him be your dread.” The same Lord of hosts Isaiah saw two chapters before, the King. Let him, the Lord of hosts, be your fear and your dread.

“And he”: the Lord of hosts, “shall be for a sanctuary; but for a stone of stumbling and for a rock of offence to both the houses of Israel, for a gin and for a snare to the inhabitants of Jerusalem.” Who is the rock of offence and the stone? The Lord of hosts. Who is that?

precepts.why: Let’s see if Peter says it is the Father, like the brother on Clubhouse. “Unto you therefore which believe he is precious: but unto them which be disobedient”, who speak on things they don’t understand, “the stone which the builders disallowed, the same is made the head of the corner, And a stone of stumbling, and a rock of offence, even to them which stumble at the word, being disobedient: whereunto also they were appointed.” Christ is that stone. So who is the Lord of hosts in Isaiah 8? Christ.

“Philip saith unto him, Lord, shew us the Father, and it sufficeth us.” Why would he ask that if Christ is his own Father? If they are the same being, one and three, he is looking at him already. Why is Philip confused?

“Have I been so long time with you, and yet hast thou not known me, Philip? he that hath seen me hath seen the Father.” What is Christ saying? I am your father: you are looking at your father. I look like my Father, and you came from me. That is why Isaiah 9 says he is the everlasting Father.

When John said it was Christ Isaiah saw, he knew what he was talking about; he wasn’t guessing. “And when he had said this, he breathed on them, and saith unto them, Receive ye the Holy Ghost.” See what that did, in Luke 24.

“And beginning at Moses and all the prophets, he expounded unto them in all the scriptures the things concerning himself.” When they read Isaiah 6 and said that is the Father, he said, no, that is me. It says LORD there, that is the Father; no, that is me too. The disciples understood who was who.

Verse 44: “That all things must be fulfilled, which were written in the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the psalms, concerning me. Then opened he their understanding, that they might understand the scriptures.” He breathed on them and opened their understanding: that in the Old Testament it is Christ all throughout, Moses and the prophets, in the volume of the book. They could tell when it was him.

An example of the scriptures referring to him. Israel was complaining for water, afraid of dying in the wilderness. “And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying, Take the rod, and gather thou the assembly together, thou, and Aaron thy brother, and speak ye unto the rock before their eyes; and it shall give forth his water.”

David said, blessed be the rock of my salvation. Does a rock have a gender? Why say his water and not its water? Because the rock represents Christ, and the disciples knew that already. Rocks have no gender. Christ said, I am the living water; the waters and the trees in Revelation are all talking about Christ. That is him in the beginning, all through the Bible, over and over again.

sense.text: “And Jacob went out from Beer–sheba, and went toward Haran. And he lighted upon a certain place, and tarried there all night, because the sun was set; and he took of the stones of that place, and put them for his pillows.”

“And he dreamed, and behold a ladder set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven: and behold the angels of God ascending and descending on it.” As he lies down, he sees angels going up and down a ladder into heaven.

“And, behold, the Lord stood above it”: is it a capital LORD? Yes. “And said, I am the Lord God of Abraham thy father, and the God of Isaac: the land whereon thou liest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed.” Who is this Lord?

precepts.why: “All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.” Some say Christ is a God, and we are all gods. No: you are not a God like Christ is a God. He is your God. There are arrogant, prideful men with fringes on who say that, and the disrespect is why they can’t understand the Bible. All things were made by him: that is what makes him our God.

“For the Lord your God is God of gods, and Lord of lords, a great God, a mighty”, like the mighty God of Isaiah 9:6, “and a terrible, which regardeth not persons, nor taketh reward.” He is a God, but he is your God.
“The Lord God of gods, the Lord God of gods, he knoweth, and Israel he shall know.” Christ is a God of gods, and his Father is a God. He is a God, but not a god like us.
“And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth.”

“He hath found out all the way of knowledge, and hath given it unto Jacob his servant, and to Israel his beloved.” Israel is God’s beloved. “Afterward did he shew himself upon earth, and conversed with men.” That is what the God of Israel did: he showed himself on earth and conversed with men. That is what John just said: the Word was made flesh and dwelt among us. The God that gave us the law is the one that came and conversed with men.

“No man hath seen God at any time”: only through visions. “The only begotten Son, which is in the bosom of the Father, he hath declared him.” So when Israel saw the pillar of fire and smoke, that was the Son.

“Philip findeth Nathanael, and saith unto him, We have found him, of whom Moses in the law, and the prophets, did write, Jesus of Nazareth.” “Can there any good thing come out of Nazareth?” He’s from the hood. “Come and see.” “Behold an Israelite indeed, in whom is no guile!” My man Nathanael. “Whence knowest thou me?” “Before that Philip called thee, when thou wast under the fig tree, I saw thee.” “Rabbi, thou art the Son of God; thou art the King of Israel.” “Thou shalt see greater things than these”: you ain’t seen nothing yet.

“Hereafter ye shall see heaven open, and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of man.” Heaven open, with the ladder, and the angels ascending and descending upon the Son of man. So who did Jacob see up there at the top of the ladder? Christ. What Jacob saw, Nathanael will see hereafter.

Baruch said he came on the earth and conversed with men; the God that gave us the law is Christ. “No man can come to me, except the Father which hath sent me draw him.” “It is written in the prophets, And they shall be all taught of God.” Who is the God that taught everyone? Christ: he came on the earth and taught the disciples, and taught us how to keep the commandments; he will magnify his law. “Every man therefore that hath heard, and hath learned of the Father, cometh unto me”: you learn of the Father through Christ.

“Not that any man hath seen the Father, save he which is of God, he hath seen the Father.” Christ is the only one who has seen the Father, and the only one who has heard his voice. The one who gave the commandments in the wilderness was Christ, always speaking on behalf of the Father. Even this is my beloved Son was an angel speaking on behalf of the Father, not the Father talking.

“For the Father judgeth no man, but hath committed all judgment unto the Son.” He has committed all judgment to his Son, and that includes teaching his laws and bringing about the end through his Son.

sense.text: “Lo, I come unto thee in a thick cloud, that the people may hear when I speak with thee, and believe thee for ever.”

“Sanctify them to day and to morrow, and let them wash their clothes, And be ready against the third day: for the third day the Lord will come down in the sight of all the people upon mount Sinai.” Be ready against the third day: so many layers to that third day, but leave it alone for now.
“Whosoever toucheth the mount shall be surely put to death: There shall not an hand touch it.” You can’t touch that mount.
“And he said unto the people, Be ready against the third day: come not at your wives.”

“And it came to pass on the third day in the morning, that there were thunders and lightnings”: the same thing as in Revelation, thunders and lightnings. “And a thick cloud upon the mount, and the voice of the trumpet exceeding loud; so that all the people that was in the camp trembled.” They were scared. “And they stood at the nether part of the mount”: at the bottom.

“And mount Sinai was altogether on a smoke, because the Lord descended upon it in fire.” That is what some of the people saw; others actually saw him sitting there. “And the whole mount quaked greatly.”
“Moses spake, and God answered him by a voice.” Moses spoke and the Lord responded, and they heard that voice.

precepts.why:
“And all the people saw the thunderings, and the lightnings, and the noise of the trumpet, and the mountain smoking: and when the people saw it, they removed, and stood afar off.” They were scared.

“And they said unto Moses, Speak thou with us, and we will hear: but let not God speak with us, lest we die.” When Moses spoke to the Lord, the Lord spoke out loud for them to hear the ten commandments. The ten commandments are the spoken commandments: the conversation between Moses and God that Israel heard. Thou shalt not kill, thou shalt not steal, thou shalt not bear false witness: they heard all of that, were terrified, and said that’s enough; Moses, from now on we will listen to you. God does not talk to you directly.

“Fear not: for God is come to prove you, and that his fear may be before your faces, that ye sin not.”

“For ye are not come unto the mount that might be touched, and that burned with fire”, as read in Exodus, “And the sound of a trumpet, and the voice of words; which voice they that heard intreated that the word should not be spoken to them any more.” Those words are the ten commandments. “(For they could not endure that which was commanded”: after the ten commandments they said, we’re good. “And so terrible was the sight, that Moses said, I exceedingly fear and quake:)”: even Moses was scared.

“But ye are come unto mount Sion, and unto the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to an innumerable company of angels, To the general assembly and church of the firstborn, which are written in heaven.” Who is the church, and who is the firstborn? Israel. We are the firstborn church, and also the church of the firstborn, Christ. Where are we written? In heaven. Are all nations written there? No.

“And to Jesus the mediator of the new covenant, and to the blood of sprinkling, that speaketh better things than that of Abel.” Abel’s sacrifice was animal blood; Christ’s blood is better than animal sacrifice.

“See that ye refuse not him that speaketh.” Who is him that speaketh? Christ. “For if they escaped not who refused him that spake on earth”: he conversed with men. “Whose voice then shook the earth: but now he hath promised, saying, Yet once more I shake not the earth only, but also heaven.” When he returns he will shake the earth and the heavens on the earth: the kingdoms, the governments ruling the earth today, the wickedness in high places. So who spoke to us in Moses’ time and gave us the laws? That is the God of the Old Testament. He created all things in Genesis 1; how can he not be the God of the Old Testament? John tells you that.

“That those things which cannot be shaken may remain”: that’s us. “Wherefore we receiving a kingdom which cannot be moved”, “For our God is a consuming fire.”

“Moreover, brethren, I would not that ye should be ignorant, how that all our fathers were under the cloud, and all passed through the sea.” Our fathers: Paul is writing to Israelites in Corinth, in Greece. “And were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea.” He dipped millions of people in water? What is that baptism? Wisdom of Solomon 19:6 shows it.

“And did all eat the same spiritual meat; And did all drink the same spiritual drink”: the laws of God. “For they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ”: the same as Numbers 20, his water. The rock that followed them and fed them was Christ: the God we dealt with in the Old Testament, in the wilderness with Moses.

“But with many of them God was not well pleased”: that God is Christ. “For they were overthrown in the wilderness. Now these things were our examples, to the intent we should not lust after evil things.” “Neither be ye idolaters”: Paul says don’t be an idolater here, so would he say be one somewhere else? “The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play”: to fornicate. “Neither let us commit fornication, as some of them committed, and fell in one day three and twenty thousand”: Numbers 25. “Neither let us tempt Christ, as some of them also tempted, and were destroyed of serpents.”

What does being baptized unto Moses mean? “For the whole creature in his proper kind was fashioned again anew”: the whole creature is Israel, fashioned again anew, born again. “Serving the peculiar commandments that were given unto them, that thy children might be kept without hurt.” That is the baptism right there: the law, serving the peculiar commandments.

“And the angel of God, which went before the camp of Israel, removed and went behind them; and the pillar of the cloud went from before their face, and stood behind them.” In front of us to lead us, behind us to protect us. Who was in that pillar? Our God is a consuming fire: that was Christ.

Who did we tempt? “And the people spake against God, and against Moses, Wherefore have ye brought us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness? for there is no bread, neither is there any water; and our soul loatheth this light bread. And the Lord sent fiery serpents among the people.” Who sent the serpents? The Lord: Christ. Paul says, neither let us tempt Christ, as some of them also tempted, and were destroyed of serpents. Whatever Christ does, his Father ordains him to do, because he gave all judgment to his Son to execute.

sense.text: “And the angel of the Lord appeared unto him in a flame of fire out of the midst of a bush.” The angel of the Lord, in a flame of fire: our God is a consuming fire. Remember that. “The bush burned with fire, and the bush was not consumed.” There was an angel talking to Moses. Everybody says that was the Father; that is not what the text says. The Bible says the angel. That is what the precepts say.

“I will now turn aside, and see this great sight, why the bush is not burnt.” What is this fire that isn’t burning the bush? Moses wanted to investigate. Most of us would run when we see something burning that isn’t burning; Moses had a different spirit.

“And when the Lord saw that he turned aside to see”: the Lord thought Moses was brave for going to see. “God called unto him out of the midst of the bush, and said, Moses, Moses. And he said, Here am I.” The Prince of Egypt did a pretty good rendition of that scene.
“Put off thy shoes from off thy feet, for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground.”
“I am the God of thy father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob. And Moses hid his face; for he was afraid to look upon God.”
“And they shall say to me, What is his name? what shall I say unto them?”

“I AM THAT I AM”: “Thus shalt thou say unto the children of Israel, I AM hath sent me unto you.” In the first person, I am that I am; in the third person, he is that he is, he is to be, the existing one. Like saying Deacon Malachiyah says, I am going to the store, or, he is going to the store: the same person, the same name. Some say Yahweh, some say other ways; just keep the commandments of God.

This is the incommunicable name: you are not supposed to toss it around. God is our Father; if your son came up and called you by your name, you would correct him. He is to be called father. The scholars put LORD and GOD in capitals so as not to keep repeating the name; even the synagogues of Satan say Hashem, the name. This was a personal conversation between Moses and the Lord. Israel didn’t throw the name around casually; they used titles. And the name itself is a schoolmaster to bring us to the real thing.

Our elders taught Yahawah, and we respect that; if you want to use it in prayer, say it, and there is no sin in that. The problem is men telling you that you have to say it or you are not saved, who can’t hold a fluent class in the Hebrew they profess, while they break every law, slander, and teach nation salvation. The forefathers had the name and dropped dead in the wilderness by the millions. We read an English book, in English. The elders in the old videos said Christ and God.

And the Lord of the Old Testament is not always the Father, if at all. The angel told Moses, I am that I am: that is the angel’s name there.

“The Lord God of your fathers”: the Lord there is he is. “The God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, hath sent me unto you: this is my name for ever, and this is my memorial unto all generations.” There will always be a God of our forefathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. He is the I am; he has been around before time, so of course it will be his name forever.

precepts.why: “Ye are my witnesses, saith the Lord, and my servant whom I have chosen: that ye may know and believe me, and understand that I am he: before me there was no God formed, neither shall there be after me.” I am he: keep that in mind.
“Thus saith the Lord the King of Israel, and his redeemer the Lord of hosts; I am the first, and I am the last; and beside me there is no God.” That is I am that I am again.

A recap of chapter 3: “And God spake unto Moses, and said unto him, I am the Lord: And I appeared unto Abraham, unto Isaac, and unto Jacob, by the name of God Almighty, but by my name Jehovah was I not known to them.” He did not appear unto them by the name I am that I am. They knew him as God Almighty, a different title. So the forefathers didn’t know the name.

“For I will pass through the land of Egypt this night, and will smite all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, both man and beast; and against all the gods of Egypt I will execute judgment: I am the Lord.” This is Christ speaking on behalf of his Father’s command.

Verse 23: “For the Lord will pass through to smite the Egyptians; and when he seeth the blood upon the lintel, and on the two side posts, the Lord will pass over the door, and will not suffer the destroyer to come in unto your houses to smite you.” The Lord and the destroyer are one and the same. The Father gave Christ the authority to execute judgment, as John 5:22 says.

And there is no scripture in this Bible showing Egyptians in Israelite houses when this took place. It is made-up nonsense from the old Easter movies.

To make it clear the Egyptians were not in Hebrew houses eating lamb with us at the Passover: “Thy servants’ trade hath been about cattle from our youth even until now”, “that ye may dwell in the land of Goshen; for every shepherd is an abomination unto the Egyptians.” That is how we got the land of Goshen: the Egyptians didn’t sit around shepherds, so they gave us our own isolated land. So how were they in our homes?

When Joseph sat down to eat with his brothers: “And they set on for him by himself, and for them by themselves, and for the Egyptians, which did eat with him, by themselves: because the Egyptians might not eat bread with the Hebrews; for that is an abomination unto the Egyptians.” The Egyptians did not sit with the Hebrews. They hated us. That is Jim Crow, segregation, the same way they separate us today and put us in the ghetto.

“For whereas they would not believe any thing by reason of the enchantments; upon the destruction of the firstborn, they acknowledged this people to be the sons of God.” When destruction came, they acknowledged us to be the sons of God.

“For while all things were in quiet silence, and that night was in the midst of her swift course”: midnight. “Thine Almighty word leaped down from heaven out of thy royal throne”: the Almighty Word is Christ. “As a fierce man of war into the midst of a land of destruction.” Christ himself came and killed the firstborn of the Egyptians and their cattle, and passed over us, at the command of his Father.

Remember Isaiah 43, I am he. “Jesus said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Before Abraham was, I am.” What did the angel say to Moses? I am that I am. Who was talking to Moses, and who gave him his name? Christ.

“Judas then, having received a band of men and officers from the chief priests and Pharisees, cometh thither with lanterns and torches and weapons”: it was late. “Jesus therefore, knowing all things that should come upon him, went forth, and said unto them, Whom seek ye? They answered him, Jesus of Nazareth. Jesus saith unto them, I am he.” I am he: Isaiah 43:10; I am that I am.

“As soon then as he had said unto them, I am he, they went backward, and fell to the ground.” Why? He gave them the same name he gave to Moses, and flexed a little. He is the same I am he of Isaiah 43, the same Lord of Exodus 6:3, the same I am of Exodus 3:14 and 15. “Then asked he them again, Whom seek ye? And they said, Jesus of Nazareth.” Christ was playing with them.

“Behold, I send an Angel before thee, to keep thee in the way, and to bring thee into the place which I have prepared.” The same angel that spoke to Moses in the bush. “Beware of him, and obey his voice, provoke him not; for he will not pardon your transgressions: for my name is in him.” My name is in him: they share the same titles.

The same is repeated in Deuteronomy, under another title: “I will raise them up a Prophet from among their brethren, like unto thee”: like Moses, a mediator. “And will put my words in his mouth”: as my name is in him. “And he shall speak unto them all that I shall command him. And it shall come to pass, that whosoever will not hearken unto my words which he shall speak in my name, I will require it of him”: beware of him, provoke him not.

He is called an angel in one chapter and the prophet in another. That is Christ.

An example of his name being in him, when Sodom and Gomorrah were destroyed: “The sun was risen upon the earth when Lot entered into Zoar.” When Lot entered a safe place, the Lord executed judgment. “Then the Lord rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from the Lord out of heaven.”

The Lord rained down fire from the Lord. There are two Lords here: the first is Christ, and the second is his Father. Christ got the authority to do it from the Lord, and he is called the Lord too. Fathers pass their names on to their sons, like a man called Mr. James after his father James. Sirach’s grandfather was Jesus and he named his son Jesus; Joseph named a son Joseph; Zacharias’ son was expected to be named after him. So the Father gave his Son his names, and our God Christ has a name, and we are going to have his name.

“And the Gentiles shall see thy righteousness, and all kings thy glory”: the heathen. “And thou shalt be called by a new name, which the mouth of the Lord shall name.” Why will we be called by a new name? All these names we use now are going to change.

“He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches; To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the hidden manna”: we don’t have that yet. “And will give him a white stone”: a diamond. “And in the stone a new name written, which no man knoweth saving he that receiveth it.”

We are going to get a new name because our Father gets his new name, and we are going to be named after him: a name we will know, because we had it before.

sense.text:
Everything gone over in this class is not regular. “Now to him that is of power to stablish you according to my gospel, and the preaching of Jesus Christ, according to the revelation of the mystery, which was kept secret since the world began.” What is the mystery kept secret since the world began? Christ. Everything in this lesson: who Christ is, his divinity, that he created everything, that he would come and die for our sin. That is the mystery told to Moses: hide these things; hide who I really am and what I have to come and do, because I don’t want everybody to understand, and be healed.

Read again at the end: who are the secrets revealed to? Us.

“But now is made manifest”: to whom? “And by the scriptures of the prophets”: written by Israel. “According to the commandment of the everlasting God, made known to all nations for the obedience of faith.” Who are all nations here? Israel: the Israelites scattered among all nations. It is not talking about every man, as some say from the Greek; precept upon precept, rightly dividing the word of truth, here a little and there a little, it is the Israelites. Stay in the Bible and never leave.

precepts.why:
“But we speak the wisdom of God in a mystery, even the hidden wisdom, which God ordained before the world unto our glory.” The class began with Christ as the wisdom of God. That hidden wisdom ordained unto our glory is Christ. He was hidden: the Pharisees, the scribes, our people couldn’t see who he really was in the scriptures.

It is the same today: our people are blinded and can’t see him in the scriptures, even many who call themselves Israel. Lo, I come in the volume of the book, it is written of me. Most of the time it is Christ speaking there, and they still think it is the Father. The Father never dealt with anyone on earth; the only one who has seen him and dealt with him is his only begotten Son.

“How that by revelation he made known unto me the mystery; (as I wrote afore in few words, Whereby, when ye read, ye may understand my knowledge in the mystery of Christ)”. The mystery is the Israelites becoming one in Christ, both houses; and Christ himself is that mystery. Do not expect everybody to understand it.

“Which in other ages was not made known unto the sons of men, as it is now revealed unto his holy apostles and prophets by the Spirit.” Nobody understood this mystery until Christ came, died, and opened the apostles’ understanding, so they could see him in the scriptures: this is Christ, this is him in Exodus. The spirit of Christ has to come and dwell in you to reveal it.

Show these things to the wise. The wise all over the world tuning in will understand; some will make videos cursing us out. Let their table become a snare and a trap: the Bible is a trap for some people, who read it and come up with stupid doctrines, because the spirit did not reveal these things to them. It was revealed to the apostles and prophets, they teach it to the people, and the wise of the people understand.

“The secret things belong unto the Lord our God: but those things which are revealed belong unto us and to our children for ever, that we may do all the words of this law.” The mysteries, revealed, belong unto us and to our children: it is ancestral, a lineage thing, ours by birthright. You can’t just come in here as a good heathen and learn the secrets of the Bible. That isn’t how this works. And for how long? For ever.
